title.en: Volume 227 Biographies 14: Chang Shu, Kang Guoli, Bo Er Jin, Ya Xi Chan, Yang Shan, Leng Geli, Sa Mu Shen Ka, Hong Niyaka, A Shan
title.raw: 卷227 列傳十四 常书 康果礼 博尔晋 雅希禅 杨善 冷格里 萨穆什喀 洪尼雅喀 阿山

sentences.zh: 常書，郭絡羅氏。

translations.literal: Chang Shu, of the Gioro clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shu belonged to the Gioro clan.

sentences.zh: 與其弟揚書，同為蘇克蘇滸河部沾河寨長。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Yang Shu were both chiefs of Zhanhe Stockade in the Sukusuhu River division.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Yang Shu both served as chiefs of Zhanhe Stockade in the Sukusuhu River division.

sentences.zh: 太祖起孤露，奮复祖父仇，歸罪尼堪外蘭，未遽訟言仇明也。

translations.literal: The Taizu, rising from orphanhood and exposure, strove to avenge his grandfather; he laid the blame on Nikhan Wailan and did not yet openly proclaim enmity toward the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu rose from orphanhood, he threw himself into avenging his grandfather, blaming Nikhan Wailan, but he had not yet openly declared war on the Ming.

sentences.zh: 明庇尼堪外蘭，宣言將築城甲班，使為滿洲主。

translations.literal: The Ming sheltered Nikhan Wailan and proclaimed that they would build the walled town of Jiaban and make him lord of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming protected Nikhan Wailan and announced that they would fortify Jiaban and install him as ruler of the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 於是旁近諸部及太祖族人，皆欲害太祖，附尼堪外蘭。

translations.literal: Thereupon the neighboring departments and Taizu's kinsmen all wished to harm Taizu and attached themselves to Nikhan Wailan.
translations.idiomatic: Then the neighboring tribes and Taizu's own clansmen all sought to destroy him and sided with Nikhan Wailan.

sentences.zh: 蘇克蘇滸河部薩爾滸城長諾米納有兄曰瓜喇，忤尼堪外蘭，尼堪外蘭譖於明，見詰治。

translations.literal: Nuomin, chief of Sarhu City in the Sukusu River Department, had an elder brother named Guala who offended Nikhan Wailan; Nikhan Wailan slandered him to the Ming, and he was seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Nuomin, chief of Sarhu in the Sukusu River tribe, had an elder brother Guala who had crossed Nikhan Wailan; Nikhan Wailan denounced him to the Ming, and Guala was taken and punished.

sentences.zh: 諾米納與常書、揚書及同部嘉木湖寨長噶哈善哈思虎相為謀曰：「與其倚此等人，何如附愛新覺羅寧古塔貝勒乎？

translations.literal: Nuomin, with Chang Shu, Yang Shu, and Gahashan Hasihu, chief of Jiamu Lake Stockade in the same department, plotted together, saying: "Rather than rely on men such as these, would it not be better to attach ourselves to Nurgaci, the Ningguta Beile of the Aisin Gioro?"
translations.idiomatic: Nuomin, Chang Shu, Yang Shu, and Gahashan Hasihu, chief of Jiamu Lake in the same tribe, took counsel together: "Why lean on such men when we could submit to Nurgaci, the Ningguta Beile of the Aisin Gioro?"

sentences.zh: 」遂相率歸太祖。

translations.literal: They thereupon led one another in submission to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: So they led their people to Taizu in a body.

sentences.zh: 太祖椎牛祭天，將與盟，常書等言於太祖曰：「我等率先來歸，幸愛如手足，毋以編氓遇我！

translations.literal: Taizu slaughtered an ox to sacrifice to Heaven and was about to covenant with them; Chang Shu and the others said to Taizu: "We have come over first—treat us as beloved as hands and feet, and do not regard us as common subjects!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sacrificed an ox to Heaven and prepared to swear alliance; Chang Shu and the others said to him: "We were the first to submit—cherish us as your own limbs, and do not treat us as mere commoners!"

sentences.zh: 」乃盟。

translations.literal: The covenant was then made.
translations.idiomatic: The oath was sworn.

sentences.zh: 既而諾米納貳於尼堪外蘭，常書等請於太祖誘而殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Nuomin turned traitor to Nikhan Wailan; Chang Shu and the others asked Taizu to lure him in and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nuomin went over to Nikhan Wailan again; Chang Shu and his brothers asked Taizu to lure Nuomin in and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 太祖以同母女弟妻揚書、噶哈善哈思虎，是歲癸未。

translations.literal: Taizu gave his uterine younger sister in marriage to Yang Shu and Gahashan Hasihu; it was the year guimao.
translations.idiomatic: That year, guimao, Taizu married his uterine sister to Yang Shu and to Gahashan Hasihu.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，太祖從叔龍敦，構太祖異母弟薩木佔，邀噶哈善哈思虎殺諸途。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Taizu's uncle Longdun, plotting with Taizu's half-brother Samuhan, invited Gahashan Hasihu and killed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year, Taizu's uncle Longdun, conspiring with his half-brother Samuhan, lured Gahashan Hasihu out and murdered him on the way.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞，大怒，欲收其骨；

translations.literal: When Taizu heard of it, he was greatly enraged and wished to recover the bones.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, hearing this, flew into a rage and set out to recover the body.

sentences.zh: 族昆弟皆與龍敦謀，不肯往。

translations.literal: The clan brothers all plotted with Longdun and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen had all sided with Longdun and refused to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 太祖率近侍數人行，太祖族叔棱敦尼之曰：「同族皆仇汝，否則汝女弟之夫何至見殺？

translations.literal: Taizu led a few close attendants on foot; his clansman-uncle Lengdun admonished him, saying: "All your kin are your enemies—else why would your sister's husband have been slain?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu went on foot with only a handful of guards; his uncle Lengdun warned him: "Your whole clan is against you—otherwise how could your sister's husband have been killed?"

sentences.zh: 宜勿往。

translations.literal: You ought not to go.
translations.idiomatic: You must not go."

sentences.zh: 」太祖勿聽，環甲躍馬，登城南橫巘，引弓疾馳。

translations.literal: Taizu would not listen; he donned armor, leapt on his horse, climbed the southern transverse ridge of the city wall, and galloped swiftly while drawing his bow.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu would not heed him. He armored himself, sprang into the saddle, rode up the south rampart, and swept along the wall with bow drawn.

sentences.zh: 向城大呼曰：「有害我者速出！

translations.literal: Facing the city he shouted loudly: "Whoever would harm me, come out at once!"
translations.idiomatic: He cried toward the town: "If any man means to harm me, let him come out now!"

sentences.zh: 」聞者憚太祖英武，不敢出，遂收其骨以歸，移置室中，解所禦冠履衣服以斂，厚葬之。

translations.literal: Those who heard feared Taizu's martial prowess and dared not come out; he thereupon recovered the bones and returned, moved them into the chamber, removed the cap, shoes, and garments he himself wore to clothe the dead, and buried him with full honors.
translations.idiomatic: They feared Taizu's valor and stayed within; he brought back the remains, laid them in his hall, stripped off his own cap and robes to dress the corpse, and buried him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 遂帥師討薩木佔及其黨訥申、萬濟漢等，為噶哈善哈思虎復仇。

translations.literal: He then led troops to punish Samuhan and his partisans Neshen, Wanji Han, and others, avenging Gahashan Hasihu.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched against Samuhan and his allies Neshen and Wanji Han, to avenge Gahashan Hasihu.

sentences.zh: 常書兄弟事太祖，分領其故部，為牛錄額真。

translations.literal: The Chang Shu brothers served Taizu, each commanding part of their former department as niru baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shu and Yang Shu served Taizu, each leading a portion of their old tribe as niru commanders.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲鑲黃旗，旋改隸鑲白旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed, they were assigned to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner, and soon after were transferred to the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Banners were established they entered the Bordered Yellow, then were moved to the Bordered White.

sentences.zh: 常書兄弟皆卒於太祖朝，揚書之喪，太祖親臨焉。

translations.literal: Both Chang Shu brothers died in Taizu's reign; at Yang Shu's funeral Taizu came in person.
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers died under Taizu; Taizu himself attended Yang Shu's obsequies.

sentences.zh: 常書子佈哈圖、察哈喇，並為牛錄額真無所表見。

translations.literal: Chang Shu's sons Buhatu and Cahała both served as niru baturu without recorded distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shu's sons Buhatu and Cahała each held a niru command, but nothing noteworthy is recorded of them.

sentences.zh: ，改隸鑲白旗。

translations.literal: , and was reassigned to the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 布哈圖事

translations.literal: The account of Buhatu
translations.idiomatic: Buhatu

sentences.zh: 察哈喇事太宗。

translations.literal: Cahała served Hong Taiji.
translations.idiomatic: Cahała served Hong Taiji.

sentences.zh: 各旗設調遣大臣，察哈喇與焉，佐正紅旗。

translations.literal: When dispatch ministers were appointed for each banner, Cahała was among them, assisting the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When each banner received its dispatch minister, Cahała was named to assist the Plain Red.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從上伐明，取遵化，薄明都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong, he followed the sovereign in campaigning against the Ming, took Zunhua, and pressed close to the Ming capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancong he followed the Khan against the Ming, seized Zunhua, and advanced to the gates of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，師還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year the army marched home.

sentences.zh: 命署固山額真，與範文程率蒙古兵守遵化。

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as gushan baturu and, with Fan Wencheng, led Mongol troops to hold Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting banner commander and, with Fan Wencheng, held Zunhua with Mongol troops.

sentences.zh: 四月，與武納格設謀，即樵採地設伏敗敵，獲馬二百餘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, with Wunage, he laid an ambush in the firewood-gathering ground and defeated the enemy, capturing more than two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he and Wunage ambushed the enemy where they gathered firewood and took over two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 明將合馬步軍四千攻大安口，復與武納格整兵奮擊，盡殲之。

translations.literal: A Ming general united horse and foot, four thousand strong, to attack Da'an Pass; again with Wunage he arrayed the troops and struck fiercely, annihilating them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When a Ming commander brought four thousand horse and foot against Da'an Pass, he and Wunage rallied their men, smashed the attack, and wiped out the force.

sentences.zh: 五月，明兵复灤州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ming troops again recovered Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Ming retook Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 貝勒阿敏等謀棄諸城，引兵出邊，令察哈喇棄遵化。

translations.literal: Beile Amin and others plotted to abandon the cities and lead the army out of the border, ordering Cahała to abandon Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Amin and others resolved to abandon the garrisons and withdraw beyond the frontier, and ordered Cahała to quit Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 會明兵已逼，察哈喇與鄂本兌等突圍出，全師以還。

translations.literal: As the Ming army had already pressed close, Cahała with Ebendui and others broke out in a sudden rush and returned with the whole force intact.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming were already upon them; Cahała, with Ebendui and others, cut his way out and brought the whole command back unscathed.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，偕總兵官冷格里、喀克篤禮伐明南海島，師次海濱，掠敵舟以渡，舟未足，駐師待之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, together with the zongbingguan Lenggeri and Kakeduli he campaigned against the Ming's southern sea islands; the army halted on the shore, seized enemy boats to cross, but the boats were insufficient and the army encamped to await more.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year he joined Lenggeri and Kakeduli in an attack on the Ming islands off the southern coast; the troops paused on the beach, commandeered enemy craft to cross, but finding too few boats, they camped to wait for more.

sentences.zh: 明兵渡海來擊，牛錄額真穆世屯戰死。

translations.literal: Ming troops crossed the sea to attack; niru baturu Mushitun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces came over the water to strike; the niru commander Mushitun fell in the fight.

sentences.zh: 察哈喇督兵力戰，別遣人沉其舟，敵還求舟不得，溺者大半。

translations.literal: Cahała supervised the troops in fierce combat and separately sent men to sink their boats; the enemy turned back seeking boats and could not find them—more than half drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Cahała drove his men hard in battle and sent others to scuttle the enemy fleet; when the Ming turned back for their boats and found none, more than half perished in the sea.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，上伐明，略歸化城，將渡河，與承政車爾格以兵五百為前鋒，具舟濟師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year the sovereign campaigned against the Ming, raided Guihua City, and was about to cross the river; with the chengzheng Cergi he took five hundred men as vanguard and prepared boats to ferry the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year, as the Khan raided toward Guihua and prepared to cross the river, Cahała and the Grand Secretary Cergi led five hundred men ahead and laid on boats to ferry the host.

sentences.zh: 十一月，與承政巴篤理使朝鮮，定職貢歲額。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, with the chengzheng Baduri he was sent to Korea to fix the annual tribute quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went with Grand Secretary Baduri to Korea and settled the yearly tribute.

sentences.zh: 九年，從貝勒多鐸攻明錦州，與固山額真阿山、甲喇額真吳拜等以兵四百為前鋒，渡大凌河，遇明兵三千，相向列陣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Beile Dodo in attacking Ming Jinzhou; with gushan baturu Ašan, jalan baturu Wubai, and others he took four hundred men as vanguard, crossed the Daling River, and met three thousand Ming troops drawn up in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he followed Beile Dodo against Jinzhou; with Ašan, Wubai, and four hundred picked men he crossed the Daling and found three thousand Ming soldiers in line of battle.

sentences.zh: 使告多鐸督諸軍繼至，明兵潰，察哈喇等分道迫擊，俘馘無算。

translations.literal: He sent word for Dodo to bring up the main army; the Ming troops broke and fled; Cahała and the others pursued on separate routes, taking captives and heads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He sent for Dodo to bring up the main force; the Ming line collapsed, and Cahała and his fellows split up in pursuit, taking prisoners and heads without number.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒。

translations.literal: The following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, he died.

sentences.zh: 布哈圖有子曰葉璽，事太宗。

translations.literal: Buhatu had a son named Ye Xi, who served Hong Taiji.
translations.idiomatic: Buhatu's son Ye Xi served Hong Taiji.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從睿親王多爾袞伐明，自青山口毀邊牆入，破薊遼總督吳阿衡軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed the Prince Regent Dorgon in campaigning against the Ming, entered by destroying the border wall at Qingshan Pass, and broke the army of the Jiliao Governor-General Wu Aheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongde he marched with Dorgon against the Ming, broke through at Qingshan Pass, and routed Jiliao Governor-General Wu Aheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，從圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed in the siege of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the siege of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從武英親王阿濟格西征。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the Prince of Warlike Merit Ajige on the western expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed Ajige, Prince of Warlike Merit, on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 二年，破李自成兵於延安，移軍下江南，至安陸，獲敵艦四，復與護軍統領哈寧阿泛江擊賊，至富池口，水陸屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the second year he broke Li Zicheng's troops at Yan'an, moved the army south of the Yangtze, reached Anlu, captured four enemy ships, and again with the hujun tongling Haninga crossed the river to strike the rebels, reaching Fuchikou; battles on land and water were repeatedly victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he shattered Li Zicheng at Yan'an, drove south of the Yangtze to Anlu, seized four rebel vessels, then with Haninga, commander of the guard, swept downriver against the rebels to Fuchikou, winning every clash on land and water.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，蘇尼特部騰機思等叛入喀爾喀，葉璽從多鐸等討之，追至布爾哈圖山，俘七人，降二十五戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, when the Sunite Tenggis and others rebelled and fled into the Khalkha, Ye Xi followed Dodo and others to punish them, pursued to Mount Burhatu, captured seven men, and received the surrender of twenty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, when the Sunite chief Tenggis rebelled into Khalkha lands, Ye Xi followed Dodo in pursuit to Burhatu Mountain, took seven prisoners, and accepted the submission of twenty-five households.

sentences.zh: 七月，師自圖拉河西行，至扎濟布拉克，遇喀爾喀土謝圖汗二子率兵二萬禦，戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the army marched west from west of the Tula River to Zhajibulake, met the Khalkha Tüsiyetü Khan's two sons leading twenty thousand men to resist, fought, and fell in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the column moved west from beyond the Tula to Zhajibulake, where the Tüsiyetü Khan's two sons met them with twenty thousand men; Ye Xi was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 葉璽時官巴牙喇甲喇章京，事聞，贈巴牙喇纛章京，予世職拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: At the time Ye Xi held the office of bayara jalan baturu; when the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted bayara banner baturu and a hereditary office of baitabuleha fan.
translations.idiomatic: He had held the rank of bayara jalan commander; on report of his death he was posthumously raised to bayara banner commander and granted the hereditary rank of baitabuleha fan.

sentences.zh: 布哈圖有孫曰辰布祿，初任牛錄額真，兼工部理事官。

translations.literal: Buhatu had a grandson named Chenbulu, who first served as niru baturu and concurrently as an official of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Buhatu's grandson Chenbulu first commanded a niru while serving on the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，從多爾袞伐明，克陽信。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he followed Dorgon in campaigning against the Ming and took Yangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongde he followed Dorgon against the Ming and captured Yangxin.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，從定西大將軍和洛輝擊賀珍漢中，從肅親王豪格討張獻忠，皆有功，授拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he followed the Dingxi Grand General Heluo in striking He Zhen at Hanzhong, and followed the Prince of Su Haoge in campaigning against Zhang Xianzhong; in both he had merit and was granted baitabuleha fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi he served under Heluo at Hanzhong against He Zhen, then under Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong, earning in both campaigns the rank of baitabuleha fan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從討鄭成功，敗其將陳六禦等於舟山，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed the campaign against Zheng Chenggong and defeated his generals Chen Liuyu and others at Zhoushan, advancing to the third-rank adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he joined the war on Zheng Chenggong, routed Chen Liuyu and others at Zhoushan, and was raised to third-rank adahafan.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 察哈喇有子曰富喇克塔，任牛錄額真、都察院理事官。

translations.literal: Cahała had a son named Fulaketa, who served as niru baturu and as an official of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Cahała's son Fulaketa held a niru command and a post on the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 崇德八年，遷工部參政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongde he was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chongde he was made vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，授正藍旗滿洲梅勒額真，旋擢本旗蒙古固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed meile baturu of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner, and soon after was promoted to Mongol gushan baturu of that banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi's first year he became meile of the Manchu Plain Blue, then was raised to Mongol banner commander of the same banner.

sentences.zh: 從睿親王多爾袞入關破李自成，追至慶都，授牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince Regent Dorgon in entering the passes to break Li Zicheng, pursued to Qingdu, and was granted the hereditary office of niru baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dorgon through the passes to crush Li Zicheng, pursued him to Qingdu, and received a hereditary niru command.

sentences.zh: 從豫親王多鐸攻潼關，自成將劉宗敏據山為陣，富喇克塔與都統拜音圖發？

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Yu Dodo in attacking Tong Pass, when Zicheng's general Liu Zongmin held the mountain in battle array, Fulaketa with the dutong Bayintu loosed [lacuna in source]
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, when Liu Zongmin, Li Zicheng's general, held the heights in order of battle, Fulaketa and the commander Bayintu opened fire with artillery

sentences.zh: 擊之，潰。

translations.literal: and struck them; they broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: and shattered the line; the rebels broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 二年，從下江南，與馬喇希等為前鋒，克揚州。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in the conquest of Jiangnan; with Malaxi and others as vanguard he took Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he marched south; as vanguard with Malaxi and others he stormed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，從貝勒博洛定浙江，克處州。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Beile Boluo in pacifying Zhejiang and took Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served under Beile Boluo in the pacification of Zhejiang and seized Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 略福建，與都統漢岱克分水關，趨泉州，下撫州及所領縣三。

translations.literal: Raiding Fujian, with the dutong Handai he took the Shuiguan Pass, pressed on Quanzhou, and reduced Fuzhou and three counties under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian he and Handai forced the Shuiguan Pass, drove on Quanzhou, and took Fuzhou and three of its counties.

sentences.zh: 加半個前程。

translations.literal: He was given half a qiancheng promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted half a step of promotion.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，坐事，解固山額真。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, for an offense he was removed from gushan baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year he was stripped of his banner command for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋從征南大將軍譚泰討金聲桓，敗賊於九江，得戰艦百餘。

translations.literal: Soon after he followed the zhengnan Grand General Tantai in campaigning against Jin Shengwan, defeated the rebels at Jiujiang, and took more than a hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Grand General Tantai against Jin Shengwan, routed the rebels at Jiujiang, and captured over a hundred war junks.

sentences.zh: 與何洛會以偏師截餉道，得糧艘二百，遂攻南昌。

translations.literal: With Heluohui he used a detached force to cut the grain route, seized two hundred grain boats, and then attacked Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: With Heluohui he took a flanking column, intercepted the supply line, seized two hundred grain barges, and laid siege to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 聲桓及王得仁以兵七萬守隘，富喇克塔以舟二十為前鋒，薄城力戰。

translations.literal: Shengwan and Wang Deren held the pass with seventy thousand men; Fulaketa took twenty boats as vanguard and pressed the city in fierce combat.
translations.idiomatic: Shengwan and Wang Deren held the defile with seventy thousand men; Fulaketa led twenty boats to the fore and fought at the walls.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊平。

translations.literal: The following year the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 師還，卒於軍，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned he died on campaign and was advanced to first-rank adahafan.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he died in the field and was posthumously raised to first-rank adahafan.

sentences.zh: 揚書有子曰達爾漢，太祖甥也。

translations.literal: Yang Shu had a son named Da'erhan, who was Taizu's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shu's son Da'erhan was Taizu's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 改隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 初為牛錄額真。

translations.literal: At first he served as niru baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He first commanded a niru.

sentences.zh: 太祖妻以女，為額駙。

translations.literal: Taizu gave him a daughter in marriage and made him an efü.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu gave him a princess and made him an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 積戰功，授一等副將世職。

translations.literal: For accumulated battle merit he was granted a first-rank vice-commander hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: For long service in the field he received a hereditary first-rank vice-commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列八大臣，領鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji took the throne, he was ranked among the eight great ministers and led the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession he was named one of the Eight Ministers and given charge of the Bordered Yellow.

sentences.zh: 從大貝勒代善伐扎魯特部，單騎逐敵，獲其台吉。

translations.literal: He followed the Great Beile Daišan in campaigning against the Jarut tribe, pursued the enemy alone on horseback, and captured their taiji.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Great Beile Daišan against the Jarut, rode out alone in pursuit, and took their taiji prisoner.

sentences.zh: 复伐棟揆部，俘塔布囊古穆楚赫爾、杜喀爾、代青多爾濟三人及其子，進三等總兵官。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the Dongkui tribe, captured the tabunang Gumuchuher, Dukar, and Daiqingdorji, the three of them and their sons, and was advanced to third-rank zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again against the Dongkui, seized the tabunang Gumuchuher, Dukar, and Daiqingdorji with their sons, and was raised to third-rank zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從伐朝鮮，克義、定、安三州，斬其府尹李莞等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed in the campaign against Korea, took the three prefectures Yi, Ding, and An, and beheaded their prefect Li Wan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancong he joined the invasion of Korea, captured Yi, Ding, and An, and slew Prefect Li Wan and others.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮國王李倧請行成，使與納穆泰等蒞盟。

translations.literal: The King of Korea Li Jong requested peace; he was sent with Namutai and others to preside over the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: King Li Jong of Korea sued for peace, and Da'erhan was sent with Namutai and others to witness the treaty.

sentences.zh: 師還，上賜宴勞之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the sovereign bestowed a feast to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the Khan held a feast in their honor.

sentences.zh: 復從伐明，攻錦州，有功。

translations.literal: Again he followed in campaigning against the Ming and attacking Jinzhou, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He served again against the Ming at Jinzhou and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 貝勒阿巴泰以賜宴不得與大貝勒同坐，屬達爾漢代奏，上使勸諭之。

translations.literal: Beile Abatai, because at the bestowed feast he could not sit with the Great Beile, charged Da'erhan to memorialize on his behalf; the sovereign had him admonish Abatai.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Abatai, denied a seat beside the Great Beile at the victory feast, had Da'erhan plead his case before the throne; the Khan sent word to soothe him.

sentences.zh: 复宴，阿巴泰又以為言，乃解達爾漢固山額真示意，旋命復任。

translations.literal: At another feast Abatai spoke again; the sovereign then removed Da'erhan from gushan baturu to make his meaning clear, but soon ordered his restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At a second feast Abatai complained again; the Khan briefly stripped Da'erhan of his banner command to make a point, then restored him at once.

sentences.zh: 三年，從伐明，圍遵化，率所部攻城西迤北，克之。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in campaigning against the Ming, besieged Zunhua, led his command to attack west and north of the city along the circuit, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the Ming campaign, besieged Zunhua, and took the northwest quarter of the wall with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 四年，蒙古敖漢、柰曼諸部兵攻昌黎，不克，命達爾漢與喀克篤禮等以兵千人往會攻，城未下，焚近郭廬舍而還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Mongol Aohan and Naiman tribes attacked Changli without success, Da'erhan was ordered with Kakeduli and others to take a thousand men to join the assault; the city was not taken, and they burned the dwellings near the outer wall and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Aohan and Naiman Mongols failed to take Changli, Da'erhan was sent with a thousand men under Kakeduli to reinforce the siege; the city held, and they burned the suburbs and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，從伐明，圍大凌河城，率所部攻城北迤東，浚壕築壘，與冷格里等環城固守。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he followed in campaigning against the Ming, besieged Dalinghe City, led his command to attack north and east of the city along the circuit, dug moats and built ramparts, and with Lenggeri and others ringed the city in a tight siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year he joined the siege of Dalinghe, threw up works on the northeast, and with Lenggeri tightened the ring about the town.

sentences.zh: 八月，城人以步騎五百出戰，達爾漢率八十人擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the city people sent five hundred foot and horse out to fight; Da'erhan led eighty men and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month five hundred defenders sallied forth; Da'erhan with eighty men drove them back.

sentences.zh: 越日，敵復出挑戰，達爾漢督所部邀擊，明兵墮壕死者百餘人。

translations.literal: The next day the enemy again came out to challenge; Da'erhan supervised his command in intercepting the attack, and more than a hundred Ming soldiers fell into the moat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they challenged again; Da'erhan met them at the ditch, and over a hundred Ming soldiers perished in the moat.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，師次哈納崖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed in campaigning against the Chahar; the army halted at Hanai Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched against the Chahar; the host camped at Hanai Cliff.

sentences.zh: 達爾漢從者盜馬，遁入察哈爾，告師至，林丹汗舉部西奔，驅歸化城富家渡黃河西遁。

translations.literal: Da'erhan's followers stole horses and fled into the Chahar, reporting that the army had arrived; Ligdan Khan led his whole tribe west in flight, driving the wealthy households of Guihua across the Yellow River to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Men in Da'erhan's train stole horses and deserted to the Chahar, warning that the army was coming; Ligdan Khan fled west with his whole people, driving Guihua's rich families across the Yellow River ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 達爾漢坐降一等副將。

translations.literal: Da'erhan was punished by reduction to second-rank vice-commander.
translations.idiomatic: Da'erhan was demoted one grade of vice-commander for the offense.

sentences.zh: 七年，明將孔有德來降，達爾漢與篇古屯兵江岸守其舟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Ming general Kong Youde came over in surrender; Da'erhan with Pangu held troops on the riverbank to guard his boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Kong Youde defected from the Ming, Da'erhan and Pangu held the riverbank to guard his fleet.

sentences.zh: 八年，復從伐察哈爾，遂略明邊，自上方堡毀邊牆入，經朔州，分。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again followed in campaigning against the Chahar, then raided the Ming border, entered by destroying the wall at Shangfang Fort, passed through Shuozhou, and divided the forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched again against the Chahar, then raided the Ming frontier, broke through at Shangfang Fort, passed Shuozhou, and split the army into raiding columns.

sentences.zh: 是歲，命免功臣徭役，達爾漢與焉，並增牛錄人戶。

translations.literal: That year, when meritorious ministers were exempted from corvée labor, Da'erhan was among them, and his niru households were also increased.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Khan exempted his great captains from corvée, Da'erhan was named among them and given additional households for his niru.

sentences.zh: 九年，上遣諸貝勒？

translations.literal: In the ninth year the khan dispatched the various beile— —
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the khan sent out the princes— —

sentences.zh: 兵至宣府右伐明，略山西，命達爾漢及阿山等出屯，牽制明寧、錦諸道兵，使不得西援。

translations.literal: — troops reached the right wing at Xuanfu to attack the Ming, raided Shanxi, and ordered Da'erhan and A Shan and others to sortie and encamp, pinning the Ming forces on the Ning and Jin routes so they could not reinforce westward.
translations.idiomatic: — their troops reached Xuanfu’s right wing on a Ming campaign, swept through Shanxi, and posted Da'erhan and A Shan in the field to tie down Ming troops on the Ning and Jin roads and block western relief.

sentences.zh: 道遇敵，擊敗之，斬明將劉應選。

translations.literal: On the march they met the enemy, defeated them, and beheaded the Ming general Liu Yingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way they met the enemy, routed them, and beheaded the Ming general Liu Yingxuan.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年五月，從武英郡王阿濟格伐明，攻順義，以所部先登，進一等總兵官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Ying of Wu, Ajige, in campaigning against the Ming, attacked Shunyi, his command was first over the wall, and he was advanced one grade to zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Chongde 1 he marched with Prince Ying Ajige against the Ming, stormed Shunyi at the head of his own men, and was raised one grade to zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 尋以順義復失，論罰​​。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Shunyi was lost again; he was judged and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shunyi soon fell again, and he was called to account.

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗等伐明，攻錦州，達爾漢坐濟爾哈朗召議禦敵不時至，嗾其僚爭功，罷固山額真，奪世職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala and others in campaigning against the Ming and attacking Jinzhou; Da'erhan was punished because when Jirhala summoned a council on meeting the enemy he did not arrive in time and incited his colleagues to vie for merit—he was removed as gushan ejen and stripped of his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Prince Zheng Jirhala’s siege of Jinzhou. Da'erhan was disgraced for arriving late when Jirhala called a council on meeting the enemy and for stirring his fellows to quarrel over credit; he lost his gushan ejen post and hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 達爾漢有子曰鄂羅塞臣，事太宗，官甲喇章京，領擺牙喇兵。

translations.literal: Da'erhan had a son, Eluosenchen, who served Hong Taiji as jalan janggin and commanded bayara troops.
translations.idiomatic: Da'erhan’s son Eluosenchen served Hong Taiji as a jalan janggin and led bayara troops.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從伐明，薄燕京，與哈寧阿共破明經略袁崇煥營。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed a campaign against the Ming, pressed Yanjing, and with Haning'a jointly broke the camp of the Ming Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he joined the Ming campaign, closed on Yanjing, and with Haning'a smashed Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan’s camp.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其善戰，授備禦。

translations.literal: Hong Taiji praised his fighting and appointed him beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji commended his valor and made him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 四年，署固山額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he served as acting gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he acted as gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒至，迎擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Following the beile, when he arrived— — met them in attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the beile; when he arrived— — he met the enemy head-on and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 五年，從伐明，圍大凌河城，屢敗城兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed a campaign against the Ming, besieged Dalinghe City, and repeatedly defeated the city troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the Ming campaign, invested Dalinghe, and repeatedly routed the garrison.

sentences.zh: 阿巴泰等守永平，明兵自開平擊敵。

translations.literal: Abtai and others held Yongping; Ming troops from Kaiping came to strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: While Abtai and others held Yongping, Ming forces from Kaiping came up to give battle.

sentences.zh: 累功，進二等阿？

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was advanced to second-rank adaha— —
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit he was advanced to second-rank adaha— —

sentences.zh: 八年，從貝勒薩哈廉略山西，明兵自崞縣至，鄂羅塞臣從第三隊先達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed Beile Sahalian in raiding Shanxi; Ming troops came from Guo County; Eluosenchen with the third column arrived first and was made adaha hafan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched with Beile Sahalian through Shanxi. When Ming troops advanced from Guo County, Eluosenchen’s third column reached the field first and he was made an adaha hafan.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從伐朝鮮，與薩穆什喀等敗其援兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the campaign against Korea and with Samushka and others defeated their relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he invaded Korea and, with Samushka and others, broke the Korean relief army.

sentences.zh: 二年，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was named to the council of state.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，從豫親王多鐸伐明，侵寧遠、錦州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year he followed Prince Yu Dodo in campaigning against the Ming and invaded Ningyuan and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year he marched with Prince Yu Dodo against the Ming and struck at Ningyuan and Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，豫親王至中後所，將與鄭親王濟爾哈朗軍會。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Prince Yu reached Zhonghou suo and was about to join the army of Prince Zheng Jirhala.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Prince Yu came to Zhonghou suo to link up with Prince Zheng Jirhala’s host.

sentences.zh: 明總兵祖大壽兵來襲，甲喇額真翁克等及從征土默特部兵先奔，鄂羅塞臣及哈寧阿等且戰且退，士卒有死傷者。

translations.literal: Ming zongbing Zu Dashou’s troops came to attack; jalan ejen Wengke and the Tümed auxiliaries fled first; Eluosenchen and Haning'a and others fought while retreating, and some soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou’s Ming force struck; Wengke the jalan ejen and the Tümed allies broke first. Eluosenchen and Haning'a fought a fighting withdrawal, and men fell.

sentences.zh: 論罰，奪世職。

translations.literal: He was judged and punished, and his hereditary office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was condemned and lost his hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，從睿親王多爾袞伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he followed Prince Rui Dorgon in campaigning against the Ming and besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he joined Prince Rui Dorgon’s siege of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，復從鄭親王濟爾哈朗伐明，圍錦州，祖大壽以步兵出戰，左翼三旗騎兵避敵勿敢擊，鄂羅塞臣與同官阿桑喜率擺牙喇兵直前奮擊，大壽乃引去。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he again followed Prince Zheng Jirhala against the Ming and besieged Jinzhou; Zu Dashou led infantry out to fight; the cavalry of the left-wing three banners shunned the enemy and dared not strike; Eluosenchen and his colleague Asanggi led bayara troops straight forward in a fierce attack, and Dashou then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he again joined Prince Zheng at Jinzhou. Dashou led foot soldiers out; the left-wing three banners’ horse troops hung back. Eluosenchen and Asanggi drove the bayara straight in, and Dashou drew off.

sentences.zh: 肅親王豪格庇三旗之未戰者，睿親王多爾袞和之，使誡鄂羅塞臣毋言戰勝皆出擺牙喇兵，亦毋言戰時未見騎兵，功罪置勿論。

translations.literal: Prince Su Hooge shielded the three banners that had not fought; Prince Rui Dorgon reconciled the matter and ordered Eluosenchen neither to say the victory was all due to bayara troops nor to say he had seen no cavalry in battle—merits and faults were left unmentioned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su Hooge covered the three banners that had held back; Prince Rui Dorgon smoothed the affair and told Eluosenchen to claim neither that bayara alone had won the day nor that no cavalry had been seen—credit and blame were quietly set aside.

sentences.zh: 明年，事聞，上令多爾袞出白金五百，豪格出白金千，畀鄂羅塞臣，進二等阿達哈哈番，擢梅勒額真。

translations.literal: The next year, when the matter came to light, the emperor ordered Dorgon to give five hundred taels of silver and Hooge one thousand, to be handed to Eluosenchen; he was advanced to second-rank adaha hafan and promoted to meire ejen.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne the following year, Dorgon was told to pay five hundred taels and Hooge a thousand to Eluosenchen; he was raised to second-rank adaha hafan and made a meire ejen.

sentences.zh: 八年，與參政巴都禮等定黑龍江。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined Bainchi and others in settling the Heilongjiang region.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he helped Bainchi and others pacify the Heilongjiang frontier.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從討李自成，克潼關，鄂羅塞臣先登。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed the expedition against Li Zicheng, took Tong Pass, and Eluosenchen was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he marched against Li Zicheng and stormed Tong Pass; Eluosenchen was first on the wall.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，命帥師駐滄州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he was ordered to command troops stationed at Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year he was posted to command at Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從武英親王阿濟格討姜瓖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he followed Prince Ying of Wu, Ajige, in suppressing Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he marched with Prince Ying Ajige against Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，擢正藍旗蒙古固山額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was promoted to Mongol gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year he became Mongol gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋兼任刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was also appointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of the Board of Punishments as well.

sentences.zh: 鄂羅塞臣，公主子，世臣，從征伐有功。

translations.literal: Eluosenchen, a princess’s son and hereditary minister, followed campaigns with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Eluosenchen was a princess’s son and hereditary servant who earned distinction on campaign.

sentences.zh: 兩遇恩詔，累進二等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: Twice favored by amnesty edicts, he was cumulatively advanced to second-rank jingqini hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Two general amnesties raised him in steps to second-rank jingqini hafan.

sentences.zh: 七年，坐讞獄徇情，罷侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was punished for judging cases with partiality and dismissed as vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he lost his vice ministership for bending judgments to favor.

sentences.zh: 八年，授都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Left Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋命專任固山。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to devote himself solely to his gushan command.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon told to hold only his banner command.

sentences.zh: 十六年，與安南將軍明安達禮帥師駐荊州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he and Pacification General Mingandali commanded troops stationed at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he and Pacification General Mingandali took station at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功犯江寧，明安達禮、鄂羅塞臣以舟師赴援，成功敗走。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong attacked Jiangning; Mingandali and Eluosenchen went with the fleet to relieve it, and Chenggong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Chenggong struck Jiangning, Mingandali and Eluosenchen sailed to its relief and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 十七年，還京，仍任都統。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to the capital and still held office as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he came back to the capital and remained commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，卒，贈太子太保，諡敏果。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he died; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Minguo.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 3 and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the temple name Minguo.

sentences.zh: 子勒貝，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Lebei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lebei is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 康果禮，先世​​居那木都魯，以地為氏。

translations.literal: Kang Guoli: his forebears dwelt in Namduru and took the place as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoli’s ancestors lived at Namduru and took that place as their clan name.

sentences.zh: 歲庚戌，太祖命額亦都將千人，徇東海渥集部，降那木都魯、綏芬、寧古塔、尼馬察四路。

translations.literal: In the year gengxu Taizu ordered Eidu to lead a thousand men, subdue the eastern-sea Woji tribe, and reduce the four routes of Namduru, Suifen, Ningguta, and Nimacha.
translations.idiomatic: In gengxu Taizu sent Eidu with a thousand men to bring in the eastern-sea Woji and to subdue the four routes of Namduru, Suifen, Ningguta, and Nimacha.

sentences.zh: 康果禮時為綏芬路屯長，與其弟喀克都裡及他屯長明安圖巴顏、泰松阿、伊勒佔、蘇爾休，明安圖巴顏子哈哈納、綽和諾，泰松阿子葉克為六牛錄，以康果禮、？

translations.literal: Kang Guoli was then tunzhang of the Suifen route; with his younger brother Kekeduli and the other tunzhang Mingantu Bayan, Taisong'a, Yilezhan, and Su'erxiu, with Mingantu Bayan’s sons Hahana and Chuohenuo and Taisong'a’s son Yekeshu they formed six niru—with Kang Guoli, Yekeshu—
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoli was tunzhang on the Suifen route. He and his brother Kekeduli, fellow tunzhang Mingantu Bayan, Taisong'a, Yilezhan, and Su'erxiu, Mingantu Bayan’s sons Hahana and Chuohenuo, and Taisong'a’s son Yekeshu made up six niru. With Kang Guoli, Yekeshu,

sentences.zh: 書等，凡十九輩，率丁壯千餘來歸。

translations.literal: — and others, nineteen generations in all, they led more than a thousand able-bodied men to submit.
translations.idiomatic: — and others—nineteen generations in all—they brought more than a thousand fighting men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖為設宴，賚以金幣，分其喀克都裡、伊勒佔、蘇爾休、哈哈納、綽和諾世領牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Taizu held a feast for them and bestowed gold and goods, appointing Kekeduli, Yilezhan, Su'erxiu, Hahana, and Chuohenuo each to inherit the office of niru ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu feasted them and gave gold and gifts, setting Kekeduli, Yilezhan, Su'erxiu, Hahana, and Chuohenuo to head their niru in succession.

sentences.zh: 旋授康果禮三等總兵官。

translations.literal: Soon Kang Guoli was appointed third-rank zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoli was soon made a third-rank zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 以貝勒穆爾哈齊女妻之，號「和碩額駙」。

translations.literal: He was given in marriage a daughter of Beile Muirhaci and styled “heshuo efü.”
translations.idiomatic: Taizu married him to a daughter of Beile Muirhaci and styled him a “heshuo imperial son-in-law.”

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed, he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After the banner system was set, he was registered in the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命三年，從上伐明，取撫順，克撫安、三岔兒等十一堡，入鴉鶻關，破清河。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianming he followed the khan in campaigning against the Ming, took Fushun, captured Fuan, Sancha'er, and eleven other forts, entered Yahuguan, and broke Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 3 he followed Taizu against the Ming, took Fushun, seized Fuan, Sancha'er, and eleven other stockades, passed Yahuguan, and stormed Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 六年，復從伐明，下瀋陽，樹雲梯先登，遂克其城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again followed a Ming campaign, took Shenyang, set a cloud ladder and was first to ascend, and thus the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched again on the Ming, took Shenyang by going up the cloud ladder first, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列十六大臣，佐正白旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, Kang Guoli was listed among the sixteen great ministers assisting the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji’s accession he was named one of the sixteen great ministers for the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋擢擺牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to bayara banner janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made bayara banner janggin.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從貝勒阿敏伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed Beile Amin in campaigning against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he joined Beile Amin’s invasion of Korea.

sentences.zh: 三年，從上伐明，入洪山口，克遵化，薄明都。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the khan in campaigning against the Ming, entered Hongshan Pass, took Zunhua, and pressed the Ming capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Taizu against the Ming, broke through Hongshan Pass, seized Zunhua, and closed on the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 上駐軍德勝門外，明督師袁崇煥入援，壁於城東南。

translations.literal: The khan halted his army outside Desheng Gate; Ming Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan came in relief and entrenched southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu camped outside Desheng Gate. Grand Secretary Yuan Chonghuan hurried to the rescue and walled up southeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 上命康果禮從諸貝勒擊之，諸貝勒逐敵迫壕，康果禮與甲喇章京郎球、漢岱等不及壕而返，並坐削爵，罰鍰，奪俘獲。

translations.literal: The khan ordered Kang Guoli to follow the beile in attacking them; the beile pursued the enemy to the moat, but Kang Guoli with jalan janggin Langqiu, Handai, and others turned back before reaching the moat—all were punished by reduction of rank, fines, and forfeiture of captives.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Kang Guoli with the princes to strike them. The princes chased the foe to the ditch, but Kang Guoli, Langqiu, Handai, and others pulled up short of the moat. All were fined, stripped of captives, and reduced in rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 子六，色虎德，繼為牛錄額真；

translations.literal: He had six sons; Sehude succeeded as niru ejen;
translations.idiomatic: Of six sons, Sehude succeeded him as niru ejen;

sentences.zh: 邁色，為擺牙喇甲喇章京，從伐明，戰塔山，沒於陣；

translations.literal: Mise served as bayara jalan janggin, followed a Ming campaign, fought at Tashan, and fell in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Mise was a bayara jalan janggin who marched against the Ming, fought at Tashan, and died in the field;

sentences.zh: 賴塔，自有傳。

translations.literal: Laita has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Laita has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 喀克都裡，與康果禮同隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: Kekeduli, like Kang Guoli, was enrolled in the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Kekeduli belonged, with Kang Guoli, to the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授三等總兵官。

translations.literal: He was first appointed third-rank zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a third-rank zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列八大臣，領正白旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, he was listed among the eight great ministers leading the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji’s accession he was one of the eight great ministers of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從伐朝鮮，有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed the Korean campaign with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he distinguished himself on the Korean campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，上伐明，圍遵化，八固山環城而攻，分隅列陣。

translations.literal: In the third year the khan campaigned against the Ming and besieged Zunhua; the eight gushan ringed the city and attacked, dividing sectors and arraying their formations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Taizu besieged Zunhua. Eight gushan encircled the walls, each holding a sector of the assault.

sentences.zh: 繼之，城遂拔。

translations.literal: Continuing thus, the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: The pressure held, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 上嘉喀克都裡造攻具如法，督兵？

translations.literal: The khan praised Kekeduli for making siege engines to regulation and supervising the troops— —
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised Kekeduli for proper siege gear and for driving the assault— —

sentences.zh: 喀克都裡所部兵薩木哈圖，樹雲梯先登，先諸軍登城，親酌金？

translations.literal: Samuhitu of Kekeduli’s command set a cloud ladder and scaled first, mounting the wall before the whole army; the khan personally poured golden— —
translations.idiomatic: Samuhitu of Kekeduli’s detachment went up the cloud ladder first and reached the wall ahead of the host. Taizu himself filled a golden— —

sentences.zh: 勞，進二等總兵官，賜號噶思哈巴圖魯，言其勇敢善戰，疾如飛鳥也。

translations.literal: — cup in reward, advanced him to second-rank zongbingguan, and granted the title Gashahabaturu, meaning brave in battle and swift as a flying bird.
translations.idiomatic: — cup for him, raised him to second-rank zongbingguan, and gave him the name Gashahabaturu—“brave in battle, swift as a bird in flight.”

sentences.zh: 薩木哈圖亦賜「巴圖魯」號，授備禦世職。

translations.literal: Samuhitu was also granted the title “Baturu” and appointed to a hereditary beiyu office.
translations.idiomatic: Samuhitu likewise received the name Baturu and a hereditary guard office.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，上复伐明，克永平，明兵潰走昌黎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the khan again campaigned against the Ming, took Yongping, and the Ming troops routed and fled to Changli.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Taizu marched again on the Ming, seized Yongping, and drove the Ming force in flight toward Changli.

sentences.zh: 上遣敖漢、柰曼、巴林、扎魯特諸部兵攻之，命喀克都裡與固山額真達爾漢等將千人繼往為助，守堅不能下，焚附城廬舍，引還。

translations.literal: The khan sent the Aohan, Naiman, Barin, and Jarut tribes to attack; he ordered Kekeduli with gushan ejen Da'erhan and others to lead a thousand men as reinforcement; the defense was firm and they could not take it, so they burned the suburbs and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent the Aohan, Naiman, Barin, and Jarut to strike Changli and sent Kekeduli with Da'erhan and a thousand men after them. The town held; they burned the outer settlements and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上既錄遵化功，察薩木哈圖猛士，心愛惜之，戒喀克都裡毋使更先登。

translations.literal: After recording the merit at Zunhua, seeing that Samuhitu was a fierce warrior, the khan cherished him and warned Kekeduli not to let him be first over the wall again.
translations.idiomatic: When the honors for Zunhua were written up, Taizu, who had taken to Samuhitu’s fierceness, told Kekeduli not to let him lead the escalade again.

sentences.zh: 及攻昌黎，薩木哈圖運木築柵，复樹雲梯欲登，聞上命罷攻，乃止。

translations.literal: At the attack on Changli, Samuhitu hauled timber to build a palisade and again set a cloud ladder intending to scale; hearing the khan’s order to halt the assault, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Changli Samuhitu dragged up timbers for a stockade and raised another ladder, but stood down when Taizu called off the assault.

sentences.zh: 上以喀克都裡不恤戰士，深詰責之。

translations.literal: Because Kekeduli did not cherish his fighting men, the khan sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sharply rebuked Kekeduli for failing to value his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，與固山額真冷格里分率左右翼步、騎兵伐明，規取南海島，徵舟於朝鮮，不至，師次海濱，不能渡，引還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year he and gushan ejen Lenggeri divided command of the left and right wings of foot and horse in campaigning against the Ming, planning to take Nanhai Island; boats were requisitioned from Korea but did not arrive; the army halted on the shore and, unable to cross, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year he and Lenggeri led the left and right wings of foot and horse against the Ming, aiming at Nanhai Island. Korea failed to send the boats; the host camped on the beach, could not cross, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 明兵邀戰，屢擊敗之，多所俘獲。

translations.literal: Ming troops intercepted them in battle; they were repeatedly defeated and many captives were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces waylaid them again and again; each clash went the Manchus’ way, and prisoners were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 八月，上复伐明，圍大凌河城，喀克都裡率所部軍城東北，城人食盡，祖大壽以城降，引還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the khan again campaigned against the Ming and besieged Dalinghe City; Kekeduli led his command northeast of the city; when the city ran out of food Zu Dashou surrendered the city, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Taizu invested Dalinghe again. Kekeduli held the northeast; when provisions failed, Dashou surrendered, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，從上伐察哈爾，與諸將分道併入，籍所俘人戶及帛、馬、牛、羊以獻，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the khan in campaigning against the Chahar; with the generals he entered by separate routes, registered the captured households and silk, horses, cattle, and sheep that were presented, and rewards were graded.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Taizu against the Chahar. The columns converged from several roads, tallied households and booty in silk, horses, cattle, and sheep, and were rewarded by rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，上詢諸貝勒大臣伐明及朝鮮、察哈爾宜何先，喀克都裡言：「宜先伐明，以承天佑、協人情，且利在神速，攻其不備。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the khan asked the beile and ministers whether to attack the Ming, Korea, or the Chahar first; Kekeduli said: “One should first attack the Ming, to receive Heaven’s favor and accord with human sentiment; moreover the profit lies in speed—strike where they are unprepared.”
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Taizu asked the princes and ministers which foe to strike first—Ming, Korea, or Chahar. Kekeduli answered: “Attack the Ming first, to keep Heaven’s blessing and men’s hearts; strike fast and hit them unready.”

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The khan praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved and took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 八年，喀克都裡家人訐喀克都裡將亡歸瓦爾喀，以財貨藏那木都魯故屯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year a member of Kekeduli’s household accused him of plotting to flee to the Warka and hiding goods in the old Namduru tun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a kinsman accused Kekeduli of planning flight to the Warka and of stashing property in the old Namduru settlement.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「喀克都里安有此？

translations.literal: The khan said: “Would Kekeduli do such a thing?”
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, “Would Kekeduli ever do that?”

sentences.zh: 果欲負朕，天必鑑之！

translations.literal: “If he truly wished to betray Us, Heaven would surely witness it!”
translations.idiomatic: “If he meant to betray me, Heaven itself would be witness!”

sentences.zh: 」以訐者付喀克都裡殺之。

translations.literal: The accuser was handed over to Kekeduli to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the accuser to Kekeduli to put to death.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，喀克都裡卒。

translations.literal: Several months later Kekeduli died.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later Kekeduli died.

sentences.zh: 其兄康果禮妻，故貝勒舒爾哈齊女，言喀克都裡謀亡去事不誣，諸子坐此不得紹封。

translations.literal: His brother Kang Guoli’s wife, a daughter of the former Beile Surhaci, said the plot to flee was not false; for this his sons could not inherit their titles.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoli’s wife, Surhaci’s daughter, later insisted the flight plot was true, and his sons were barred from succession on that account.

sentences.zh: 哈哈納，亦那木都魯氏，明安圖巴顏子也。

translations.literal: Hahana, also of the Namduru clan, was the son of Mingantu Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Hahana, likewise of the Namduru line, was Mingantu Bayan’s son.

sentences.zh: 隸滿洲鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: He was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged to the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 初與伊勒佔、蘇爾休同授備禦。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed beiyu together with Yilezhan and Su'erxiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made a guard officer along with Yilezhan and Su'erxiu.

sentences.zh: 太祖妻以宗女。

translations.literal: Taizu gave him a princess of the clan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu married him to a clanswoman of imperial rank.

sentences.zh: 尋從伐烏喇，被數創，力戰敗敵。

translations.literal: Soon he followed a campaign against Ula, suffered many wounds, and fought fiercely to defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marched on Ula, took many wounds, and fought through to victory.

sentences.zh: 上命將所部出駐賽明吉，未至，其戍兵叛亡，守將瑪爾圖追弗及。

translations.literal: The khan ordered him to lead his command out to garrison Saimingji; before he arrived the garrison troops rebelled and fled; the defending commander Maltu pursued but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent him to take his men to Saimingji. Before he arrived the garrison mutinied and ran; Commandant Maltu gave chase but could not catch them.

sentences.zh: 哈哈納聞之，兼程疾進，斬三百餘級，收男婦五百餘以還。

translations.literal: When Hahana heard of it he pressed on by forced marches, beheaded more than three hundred, and brought back more than five hundred men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Hahana heard and hurried on by night marches, killed more than three hundred, and recovered over five hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 上賜以所得叛渠及鞍馬、弓矢。

translations.literal: The khan bestowed on him the rebel leaders taken and saddles, horses, bows, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu gave him the rebel chiefs that were seized, with saddles, horses, bows, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 天命四年三月，明經略楊鎬部諸將四路來攻，上督諸貝勒出禦，破之，遂進克開原、鐵嶺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Tianming the Ming Grand Secretary Yang Hao’s generals came in four columns to attack; the khan supervised the beile in going out to meet them, defeated them, and then advanced to take Kaiyuan and Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianming 4 Grand Secretary Yang Hao’s Ming generals advanced in four columns. Taizu led the princes out to meet them, broke them, and went on to take Kaiyuan and Tieling.

sentences.zh: 哈哈納皆在軍有功。

translations.literal: Hahana had merit in every campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Hahana distinguished himself in every campaign he joined.

sentences.zh: 六年，從攻遼陽，與博爾晉伺敵城下，敗其援兵；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Liaoyang; with Bo'erjin he watched for the enemy below the walls and defeated their relief force;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the assault on Liaoyang. He and Bo'erjin lay in wait beneath the walls, routed the Ming relief army,

sentences.zh: 復分攻沙嶺城，破援兵自廣寧至者。

translations.literal: again he was detached to attack Shaling fortress and broke the relief troops coming from Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: then was sent again against Shaling and shattered the reinforcements marching from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，設各旗調遣大臣，以哈哈納佐鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, dispatch ministers were appointed for each banner; Hahana was made assistant to the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession each banner received a dispatch minister; Hahana assisted the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，帥師略錦州，進攻寧遠，明兵驟至，哈哈納馬殕，徒步益奮擊，卒破明兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he commanded troops to raid Jinzhou and advance on Ningyuan; Ming forces suddenly arrived; Hahana's horse was killed, yet on foot he fought all the harder and finally broke the Ming army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he led a raid toward Jinzhou and pushed on to Ningyuan. Ming troops rushed up; his horse was killed, but he fought on foot with redoubled fury and at last routed them.

sentences.zh: 城海州，明兵來爭，哈哈納以所部首當敵，敵潰走。

translations.literal: When Haizhou was being walled, Ming troops came to contest it; Hahana led his command in the van against the enemy, who broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: While Haizhou was being fortified Ming forces came to dispute it. Hahana put his men in the forefront, and the enemy scattered.

sentences.zh: 复援耀州，解其圍，逐敵，獲馬三十。

translations.literal: Again he relieved Yaozhou, lifted the siege, pursued the enemy, and captured thirty horses.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Yaozhou, broke the siege, drove the foe, and took thirty horses.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從武英郡王阿濟格伐明，入長城，克昌平、涿州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Ying Ajige in campaigning against the Ming, entered the Great Wall, and took Changping and Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he marched with Prince Ying Ajige against the Ming, crossed the Great Wall, and captured Changping and Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 創發，病廢，致仕。

translations.literal: Old wounds reopened, illness disabled him, and he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: His wounds reopened, illness laid him low, and he retired.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 子費揚古，事聖祖。

translations.literal: His son Feiyanggu served the Kangxi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feiyanggu served the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 以佐領從軍，討吳三桂。

translations.literal: As an assistant commandant he followed the army to suppress Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: As an assistant commandant he campaigned against Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 師次荊州，戰宜昌，戰永興，皆捷；

translations.literal: The army halted at Jingzhou; battles at Yichang and at Yongxing were all victorious;
translations.idiomatic: The force stopped at Jingzhou; fights at Yichang and Yongxing were all won;

sentences.zh: 攻常寧、耒陽，先驅。

translations.literal: in attacks on Changning and Leiyang he led the van.
translations.idiomatic: and at Changning and Leiyang he spearheaded the assault.

sentences.zh: 累遷鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner Chinese Brigade.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 綽和諾，亦隸鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: Chuohenuo likewise belonged to the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chuohenuo also served in the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 其初歸太祖，別率所部百人偕，太祖賚予甚厚。

translations.literal: When he first submitted to Taizu he brought a separate command of a hundred men with him, and Taizu rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: On first submitting to Taizu he came with a hundred men of his own command, and Taizu lavished gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 從太祖征伐，臨陣衷綿甲，奮起直前，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Following Taizu on campaign, he would bind cotton armor about himself in battle, spring forward, and sweep all before him.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaigns he wore cotton armor under his gear, charged straight ahead, and nothing could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 歲辛亥，從何和禮伐呼爾哈部，克扎庫塔城。

translations.literal: In the year xinhai he followed He Heli in attacking the Hurka tribe and took Zhakuta fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year he joined He Heli against the Hurka and captured Zhakuta.

sentences.zh: 天命四年，擊明總兵馬林尚間崖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianming he struck Ming Commander Ma Lin at Shangjianya.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 4 he fought Ming Commander Ma Lin at Shangjianya.

sentences.zh: 六年，取瀋陽、遼陽，並有功，授游擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he helped take Shenyang and Liaoyang, all with merit, and was appointed guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he shared in the capture of Shenyang and Liaoyang and was made a guerrilla officer.

sentences.zh: 帥師戍科木索、寧古塔。

translations.literal: He led troops to garrison Kemusuo and Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded garrisons at Kemusuo and Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 掠輜重亡去，綽和諾追及海濱，斬就善，並殲其黨，上命以所獲輜？

translations.literal: Some men plundered the baggage train and fled; Chuohenuo pursued them to the seashore, beheaded Jiushan, and annihilated his band; the khan ordered the captured baggage train used to —
translations.idiomatic: Men who had looted the supply train fled; Chuohenuo overtook them on the coast, killed Jiushan, and wiped out his followers; the khan had the captured train used to —

sentences.zh: 有就善者，戕守吏，率重犒之。

translations.literal: There had been a Jiushan who murdered the garrison officer and led the heavy baggage away to plunder; he was rewarded for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiushan had killed the garrison officer and led the looters off with the train; the khan rewarded the victors with what was taken.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列十六大臣，佐鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, Chuohenuo was listed among the sixteen great ministers assisting the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession he became one of the sixteen great ministers for the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰五年，從上伐明，圍大凌河城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancong he followed the khan in campaigning against the Ming and besieged Dalinhe fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 5 he followed the khan against the Ming and invested Dalinhe.

sentences.zh: 明監軍道迎擊，力戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: The Ming supervisor-general came out to meet the attack; he fought fiercely and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming supervisor-general met them head-on; Chuohenuo fought to the end and died on the field.

sentences.zh: 上厚卹其家，進？

translations.literal: The khan lavished compensation on his family and advanced his line to —
translations.idiomatic: The khan richly compensated his household and promoted his line to —

sentences.zh: 張春、總兵吳襄等率兵萬餘自錦州來援，綽和諾先世職一等參將。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, Commander Wu Xiang, and others led more than ten thousand men from Jinzhou to relieve the siege; Chuohenuo was granted the hereditary office of First-rank Assistant General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, Commander Wu Xiang, and others marched more than ten thousand men from Jinzhou to relieve the fortress; Chuohenuo was granted the hereditary rank of First-rank Assistant General.

sentences.zh: 無子，其兄翁格尼襲，以新附呼爾哈百人益所轄牛錄。

translations.literal: He had no son; his elder brother Wenggeni succeeded, and a hundred newly submitted Hurka were added to the niru under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Without a son, his elder brother Wenggeni inherited, and a hundred newly submitted Hurka were added to his niru.

sentences.zh: 旋以翁格尼才不勝，改授其子富喀禪。

translations.literal: Soon, because Wenggeni's ability was unequal to the post, the office was transferred to his son Fukucan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenggeni proved unequal to the duty, the post passed to his son Fukucan.

sentences.zh: 富喀禪初以擺牙喇壯達事太宗。

translations.literal: Fukucan first served Hong Taiji as a bayara dartachi.
translations.idiomatic: Fukucan began as a bayara dartachi under Hong Taiji.

sentences.zh: 大凌河之役，深入敵陣，綽和諾戰死，富喀禪亦被創墮馬，裹創步戰，搴敵纛；

translations.literal: At the battle of Dalinhe he plunged deep into the enemy formation; Chuohenuo was killed in action, and Fukucan too was wounded and fell from his horse, yet binding his wounds he fought on foot and tore down an enemy banner;
translations.idiomatic: At Dalinhe he drove deep into the enemy ranks. Chuohenuo fell; Fukucan was wounded and thrown from his horse, but wrapping his wounds he fought on foot and pulled down an enemy standard;

sentences.zh: 擺牙喇壯達瑤奎亦墮馬，富喀禪复前援，與俱歸。

translations.literal: the bayara dartachi Yao Kui also fell from his horse; Fukucan went forward again to rescue him, and both returned.
translations.idiomatic: bayara dartachi Yao Kui also fell; Fukucan went back to help him, and both came out alive.

sentences.zh: 八年，攻大同，復被創，仍奮進克敵寨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attacked Datong, was wounded again, yet pressed on and took the enemy stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year at Datong he was wounded again but still stormed and took an enemy fort.

sentences.zh: 是歲代其父為牛錄額真，襲職。

translations.literal: That year he replaced his father as niru ejen and inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he succeeded his father as niru ejen.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the campaign against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he joined the Korean campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，授工部理事官，兼甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed supervising officer of the Board of Works and concurrently jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became a supervising officer of the Board of Works and jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 從豫親王多鐸伐明，攻寧遠，敗敵中後所城西。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Yu Dodo in campaigning against the Ming, attacked Ningyuan, and defeated the enemy west of Zhonghousuo.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Prince Yu Dodo against the Ming, struck Ningyuan, and beat the foe west of Zhonghousuo.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關擊李自成，加半個前程。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes to strike Li Zicheng and was given half a frontier honor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he crossed the passes against Li Zicheng and received half a frontier honor.

sentences.zh: 三年，授西安駐防總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed garrison commandant at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made garrison commandant at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 自成餘黨劉文炳、郭君鎮等​​掠延安、慶陽。

translations.literal: Remnants of Li Zicheng's forces—Liu Wenbing, Guo Junzhen, and others—raided Yan'an and Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's remnant bands under Liu Wenbing, Guo Junzhen, and others plundered Yan'an and Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，富喀禪帥師討之，逐賊三水，斬君鎮；

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year Fukucan led troops against them, drove the bandits to Sanshui, and beheaded Junzhen;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year Fukucan took the field, chased the rebels to Sanshui, and killed Junzhen;

sentences.zh: 別遣游擊胡來覲、守備徐國崇等逐文炳至宜君藍莊溝，獲之，俘斬其黨略盡。

translations.literal: he separately dispatched guerrilla officer Hu Laijing, garrison commandant Xu Guochong, and others to pursue Wenbing to Yijun Lanzhuanggou, capture him, and execute nearly all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: and sent guerrilla Hu Laijing and garrison commandant Xu Guochong after Wenbing to Yijun Lanzhuanggou, where they took him and cut down most of his band.

sentences.zh: 五年，回民米喇印、丁國棟等陷河州為亂，富喀禪與總督孟喬芳遣兵攻討，諸回皆受撫，而喇印复叛，陷甘州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Hui leaders Milayin, Ding Guodong, and others seized Hezhou in revolt; Fukucan and Governor Meng Qiaofang sent troops to attack; all the Hui submitted to pacification, but Layin rebelled again and took Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Hui Milayin and Ding Guodong seized Hezhou. Fukucan and Governor Meng Qiaofang sent forces; the Hui submitted, then Layin rose again and took Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 富喀禪帥師進攻，深溝高壘相持，賊出城來犯，戰輒勝，並殲其樵採者。

translations.literal: Fukucan led troops to press the attack; with deep trenches and high ramparts the two sides faced each other; whenever the rebels came out of the city to attack, battle was invariably won, and their wood-gatherers were also wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Fukucan besieged them behind deep ditches and high walls; each sortie was beaten back and their foraging parties were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 城既下，馘喇印。

translations.literal: Once the city fell, Layin was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he slew Layin.

sentences.zh: 國棟又與？

translations.literal: Guodong again joined —
translations.idiomatic: Ding Guodong again joined —

sentences.zh: 回土倫泰等陷肅州，遣副將馬寧、張勇討平之。

translations.literal: Hui noble Tuluntai and others in seizing Suzhou; he dispatched Deputy Generals Ma Ning and Zhang Yong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuluntai and other Hui leaders in taking Suzhou; Fukucan sent Deputy Generals Ma Ning and Zhang Yong to crush them.

sentences.zh: 六年，姜瓖以大同叛，旁近郡縣皆陷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang rebelled at Datong and neighboring prefectures and counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang rebelled at Datong and the surrounding districts collapsed.

sentences.zh: 富喀禪遣諸將根特、杜敏赴援，戰猗氏，獲瓖登方；

translations.literal: Fukucan sent Generals Gent and Du Min to relieve them; at Yishi they captured Jiang's younger brother Dengfang;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gent and Du Min to the rescue; at Yishi they seized Jiang's brother Dengfang;

sentences.zh: 戰合水，斬瓖將劉宏才。

translations.literal: at Heshui they beheaded Jiang's general Liu Hongcai.
translations.idiomatic: at Heshui they killed Jiang's general Liu Hongcai.

sentences.zh: 論功，遇恩詔，累進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit, on an imperial grace amnesty, he was repeatedly advanced to First-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: For his services, on an imperial grace amnesty, he rose to First-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 聖祖？

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor —
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor —

sentences.zh: 所署監軍道即位，改西安駐防總管為將軍，富喀禪任事如故。

translations.literal: ascended the throne, the Xi'an garrison commandant was made a general, and Fukucan continued in his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: took the throne, the Xi'an garrison post became a generalship, and Fukucan kept his command.

sentences.zh: 時自成餘黨李來亨、郝搖旗、袁宗第等屯歸州、興山間。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng's remnant leaders Li Laiheng, Hao Yaoqi, Yuan Zongdi, and others were encamped between Guizhou and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Laiheng, Hao Yaoqi, Yuan Zongdi, and other rebel holdouts camped between Guizhou and Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，上遣將往討，命富喀禪與總督李國英、副都統杜敏等會師，戰於陳家坡，賊潰遁，進至黃草坡，復大敗之，進三等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi the court sent generals to suppress them and ordered Fukucan to join forces with Governor Li Guoying, Vice Commander-in-Chief Du Min, and others; at Chenjiapo the bandits were routed and fled; advancing to Huangcaopo they were again heavily defeated, and he was promoted to Third-rank Jingqiniha.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 the court sent armies against them; Fukucan joined Governor Li Guoying and Du Min, routed the rebels at Chenjiapo, crushed them again at Huangcaopo, and was raised to Third-rank Jingqiniha.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 子穆成額，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Mucheng'e has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mucheng'e is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 葉克書，輝和氏，尼瑪察部長泰松阿子也。

translations.literal: Yekeshu, of the Hoho clan, was the son of Taisong'a, chief of the Nimanča tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yekeshu of the Hoho line was the son of Nimanča chief Taisong'a.
