translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, his younger brother Namutai was made one of the eight great ministers heading the banner, while Lenggeri was listed among the sixteen great ministers assisting him.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession Namutai headed the banner among eight ministers; Lenggeri assisted among sixteen.

sentences.zh: 蒙古扎魯特部貳於明，大貝勒代善等帥師討之，冷格里及甲喇額真阿山將六百人為前鋒，略喀爾喀巴林部，逐守卒，縱火燎原，張軍勢，轉戰而前，獲扎魯特部貝勒巴克等十四人，俘二百七十一，掠駝、馬、牛、羊三千九百四十有二。

translations.literal: The Mongol Zhalut tribe turned to the Ming; Grand Beile Daisan and others led troops to punish them; Lenggeri and Jalan Ejen Ashan commanded six hundred men as vanguard, raided the Khalkha Balin tribe, drove off the garrison, set fires across the steppe to display army strength, fought forward in rotation, captured fourteen men including Zhalut Beile Bake, took two hundred seventy-one prisoners, and seized three thousand nine hundred forty-two camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Zhalut, Lenggeri and Ashan led six hundred vanguard men, raided Balin, took Bake and 271 captives, and huge herds.

sentences.zh: 師還，上率諸貝勒大臣迎勞，進三等總兵官。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the khan with all beile and ministers went out to welcome and reward them; he was advanced to Third-rank zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Taizu welcomed him and made him Third-rank zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從貝勒阿敏等伐朝鮮，夜引兵八十人襲明邊，一夕入六堠，盡俘其堠卒，遂襲義州，克之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed Beile Amin and others against Korea; by night he led eighty men in a surprise raid on the Ming frontier, in one night entered six beacon stations, captured all the beacon soldiers, then struck Yizhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he raided six Ming beacons in one night and took Korean Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 論功，進一等總兵官。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to First-rank zongbingguan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became First-rank zongbingguan.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，明兵自海島移屯朝鮮鐵山，冷格里率精兵攻之，多所斬馘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Ming troops moved their camp from the sea island to Korean Tieshan; Lenggeri led picked troops to attack and took many heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he struck Ming at Korean Tieshan and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 九月，從揚古利率兵逐逃人雅爾古，遇毛文龍部卒以採葠至者，俘數十人以還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Yangguli in pursuing fugitives to Ya'ergu; he met Mao Wenlong's soldiers coming to gather herbs, captured several tens, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he captured dozens of Mao Wenlong's foragers.

sentences.zh: 四年，納穆泰以棄灤州黜，擢冷格里為八大臣，領本旗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Namutai was removed for abandoning Luanzhou; Lenggeri was raised to one of the eight great ministers and headed the banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Namutai fell for losing Luanzhou and Lenggeri took his place among eight ministers.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，與喀克篤禮分將左右翼兵伐南海島，有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, with Kakeduli he divided command of left and right wing troops in campaigning against the southern sea island, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year he and Kakeduli raided the southern sea island.

sentences.zh: 八月，太宗伐明，冷格里從，圍大凌河城，冷格里以所部軍於城西北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Hong Taiji campaigned against the Ming; Lenggeri followed and besieged Dalinhe; Lenggeri stationed his command northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month at Dalinhe he held the northwest with his men.

sentences.zh: 上招明總兵祖大壽降，大壽未？

translations.literal: The khan summoned Ming Commander Zu Dashou to surrender; Zu Dashou had not yet —
translations.idiomatic: Taizu called Zu Dashou to surrender; Dashou had not yet —

sentences.zh: ，先使裨將韓棟出謁，出冷格里所守門。

translations.literal: first sent his deputy Han Dong out to audience; he went out through the gate Lenggeri guarded.
translations.idiomatic: sent Deputy Han Dong out through Lenggeri's gate.

sentences.zh: 冷格里令軍士戎服執戟，立營門內外，示棟軍容。

translations.literal: Lenggeri ordered the soldiers in battle dress holding halberds to stand inside and outside the camp gate to display army bearing to Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Lenggeri lined his gate with armed men to impress Han Dong.

sentences.zh: 棟既謁上還，將入城，冷格里呵使止門外，問姓名，審形貌，然後令入。

translations.literal: When Dong had paid his respects and returned, about to enter the city, Lenggeri shouted for him to halt outside the gate, asked his name, examined his appearance, and only then allowed him in.
translations.idiomatic: Lenggeri halted Han Dong at the gate, questioned him, then let him pass.

sentences.zh: 棟具以語大壽，大壽怵我軍嚴整，乃決降。

translations.literal: Dong reported all this to Zu Dashou; Zu Dashou, fearing our army's strict order, then resolved to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dong told Dashou of our discipline, and Dashou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，從貝勒岳託等將右翼兵伐明，取旅順，師還，上迎勞如初。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year he followed Beile Yoto and others commanding the right-wing troops against the Ming, took Lüshun, and when the army returned the khan welcomed and rewarded them as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he took Lüshun with Yoto and was welcomed as before.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，冷格里有疾，十二月，上親至其第視疾。

translations.literal: That winter Lenggeri fell ill; in the twelfth month the khan came in person to his residence to visit his illness.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Taizu visited his sickbed in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 上臨其喪，哭之慟，駕還，設幄於丹墀，坐而歎息，漏下二鼓始入宮。

translations.literal: The khan came to his funeral and wept bitterly; when the carriage returned, a tent was set on the red steps; he sat sighing until the second watch before entering the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wept at his funeral and sat sighing on the palace steps until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 明年，上行幸，道經其墓，下馬酹而哭之。

translations.literal: The next year, on a tour, passing his tomb, the khan dismounted, poured a libation, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Taizu poured wine and wept at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，追諡武襄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was posthumously titled Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 he received posthumous name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 子穆成格。

translations.literal: His son Muchengge.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Muchengge.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，從伐明，克永平四城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against the Ming and took the four cities of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 he took the four Yongping cities.

sentences.zh: 薄明都，明侍郎劉之綸率兵出禦，戰敗，所將兵盡殲，之綸匿石岩下，穆成格射殺之。

translations.literal: Pressing the Ming capital, Ming Vice Minister Liu Zhilun led troops out to meet them, was defeated, and his entire command was annihilated; Zhilun hid beneath a rock cliff; Muchengge shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ming capital Liu Zhilun was destroyed; Muchengge shot him hiding under the rocks.

sentences.zh: 八年，襲一等總兵官，尋改一等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he inherited First-rank zongbingguan and soon was changed to First-rank angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he inherited First-rank zongbingguan, soon angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 官至刑部左參政。

translations.literal: He reached the office of left vice minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became left vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 卒，子穆赫林，襲。

translations.literal: He died; his son Muhelin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Muhelin inherited.

sentences.zh: 順治初，改一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi it was changed to First-rank Jingqiniha.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi the rank became First-rank Jingqiniha.

sentences.zh: 恩詔，累進一等伯。

translations.literal: On imperial grace amnesties he was repeatedly advanced to First-rank count.
translations.idiomatic: Grace amnesties raised him to First-rank count.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，其孫吉當阿襲，復為一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period his grandson Jidang'a succeeded and again held First-rank Jingqiniha.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi his grandson Jidang'a inherited as First-rank Jingqiniha.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，定封一等子。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period the fief was fixed as First-rank viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong the rank was fixed as First-rank viscount.

sentences.zh: 納穆泰，揚古利幼弟，其母襁負來歸者也。

translations.literal: Namutai was Yangguli's youngest brother, carried in his mother's arms when they came over.
translations.idiomatic: Namutai was Yangguli's youngest brother, brought over as an infant.

sentences.zh: 少從太祖征伐。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Taizu on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Taizu from youth.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，擢為八大臣，領本旗，以篤義貝勒巴雅喇子拜音圖及其兄冷格里為十六大臣佐之。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded he was promoted to one of the eight great ministers, headed the banner, with Dutiful Prince Bayara's son Bayintu and his elder brother Lenggeri as sixteen ministers assisting.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession he became one of eight ministers; Bayintu and Lenggeri assisted.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從伐朝鮮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he invaded Korea.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，從伐明，攻遵化，率所部軍其城西北。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he followed the campaign against the Ming and attacked Zunhua, leading his command at the northwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third winter he attacked Zunhua at the northwest.

sentences.zh: 四年春，复克永平，降遷安，下灤州，是為永平四城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he again took Yongping, reduced Qian'an, and took Luanzhou—the four cities of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth spring he retook Yongping, Qian'an, and Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，命貝勒阿敏督諸將戍守，納穆泰與圖爾格、庫爾？

translations.literal: When the army returned, Beile Amin was ordered to supervise the generals in garrison defense; Namutai with Turgut, Ku'er —
translations.idiomatic: On the return Amin garrisoned the cities; Namutai with Turgut and Ku'er —

sentences.zh: 、高鴻中率正黃、正紅、鑲白三旗分守灤州。

translations.literal: and Gao Hongzhong led the Plain Yellow, Plain Red, and Bordered White banners in divided defense of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Gao Hongzhong held Luanzhou for three banners.

sentences.zh: 明經略孫承宗銳意复四城，四月，遣兵攻灤州，不能克而退。

translations.literal: Ming Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong was keen to recover the four cities; in the fourth month he sent troops to attack Luanzhou but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chengzong tried to retake the four cities in the fourth month but failed at Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，監軍道張春、監紀官邱禾嘉，總兵祖大壽、馬世龍、楊紹基，副將祖大樂、祖可法、張弘謨、劉天祿、曹恭來攻，納穆泰與圖爾格分門而守，矢石競發，出精銳繞城搏戰，驅敵出壕外。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Grand Coordinator Zhang Chun, supervising secretary Qiu Hejia, commanders Zu Dashou, Ma Shilong, and Yang Shaoji, deputy commanders Zu Dale, Zu Kefa, Zhang Hongmo, Liu Tianlu, and Cao Gong came to attack; Namutai and Turgut defended by separate gates; arrows and stones flew; picked troops were sent out to circle the city and fight hand to hand, driving the enemy beyond the moat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhang Chun and Zu Dashou assaulted Luanzhou; Namutai and Turgut held the gates and drove them from the moat.

sentences.zh: 誠、孟弢悉敵复突至，攻納穆泰所守門，焚城樓，或執纛緣雲梯先登，我兵阿玉什斬之，奪其纛，敵稍卻，求援於阿敏。

translations.literal: Cheng, Meng Xian, and all the enemy again suddenly arrived and attacked the gate Namutai guarded, burning the gate tower; some seized banners and climbed cloud ladders first; our soldier Ayushi cut them down and seized their banners; the enemy drew back slightly and begged aid from Amin.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy burned Namutai's gate tower; Ayushi cut down ladder climbers; they begged Amin for help.

sentences.zh: 阿敏守永平，使巴篤禮以數百人往，夜突圍入城。

translations.literal: Amin held Yongping and sent Baduli with several hundred men who in the night broke through the encirclement and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Amin sent Baduli with hundreds through the siege by night.

sentences.zh: 敵以砲攻，我兵不能禦，守四日夜，棄城奔永平就阿敏。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked with cannon; our troops could not withstand it; after defending four days and nights they abandoned the city and fled to Yongping to join Amin.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon fire forced them out after four days; they fled to Yongping.

sentences.zh: 阿敏旋引師還，永平四城復入於明。

translations.literal: Amin soon led the army back, and the four Yongping cities again fell to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Amin withdrew and the four cities returned to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 納穆泰坐論死，上命宥之，奪官，籍其家。

translations.literal: Namutai was sentenced to death by discussion; the khan ordered him spared, stripped of office, and his household property registered.
translations.idiomatic: Namutai was condemned to death but spared, cashiered, and his property seized.

sentences.zh: 五年，將兵入明邊逐逋，斬六人，執九人以歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he led troops into the Ming frontier to pursue fugitives, beheaded six, and brought back nine captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he raided the Ming border, killed six, and took nine prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明寧遠人張士粹來降，詭言明築大凌河城，使納穆泰與圖爾格將千人往诇之，還言士粹等言妄，悉誅之。

translations.literal: A Ningyuan Ming man Zhang Shicui surrendered and falsely reported that the Ming were building Dalinhe; Namutai and Turgut were sent with a thousand men to scout; on return they said the tale was false and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicui lied about Dalinhe; Namutai and Turgut scouted, exposed the lie, and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 尋擢兵部承政，授游擊世職。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of War and granted the hereditary office of guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of War with hereditary guerrilla rank.

sentences.zh: 復與圖爾格略錦州、松山。

translations.literal: Again with Turgut he raided Jinzhou and Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Jinzhou and Songshan with Turgut again.

sentences.zh: 八年，改官制，授固山額真、三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the official system was changed; he was appointed gushan ejen and Third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became gushan ejen and Third-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 秋，從上伐明，自上方堡入，八月，克靈丘縣王家莊，先登有功。

translations.literal: In autumn he followed the khan against the Ming, entering from Shangfang Fort; in the eighth month he took Wangjiazhuang in Lingqiu, first to ascend with merit.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he entered from Shangfang Fort and was first up at Wangjiazhuang.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，命貝勒多爾袞將萬人，收察哈爾林丹汗子額爾克孔果爾額哲，納穆泰將右翼，圖爾格將左翼。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year Beile Dorgon commanded ten thousand men to receive Lindan Khan's son Erkezhe; Namutai commanded the right wing and Turgut the left.
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon received Chakhar princes; Namutai led the right wing and Turgut the left.

sentences.zh: 師還，入明境，自平魯略代州，至崞縣出邊，納穆泰、圖爾格以兵千人殿。

translations.literal: Returning through Ming territory from Pinglu via Daizhou to Guoxian, Namutai and Turgut with a thousand men formed the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Ming lands, Namutai and Turgut guarded the rear with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 明總兵祖大壽率馬步兵三千人追至，？

translations.literal: Ming Commander Zu Dashou led three thousand horse and foot in pursuit to —
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou pursued with three thousand men —

sentences.zh: ，獲人畜七萬六？

translations.literal: —, capturing men and livestock numbering seventy-six thousand —
translations.idiomatic: — and took seventy-six thousand head —

sentences.zh: 圖爾格奮擊破之；

translations.literal: Turgut struck fiercely and broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Turgut charged and broke them;

sentences.zh: 潰兵合馬步五百餘據台為陣，納穆泰麾兵圍攻，盡殲其千二百。

translations.literal: broken troops of five hundred horse and foot held a platform; Namutai encircled and annihilated all twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: five hundred Ming held a platform; Namutai surrounded and killed twelve hundred.

sentences.zh: 功，加三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: For merit he was given Third-rank meiren janggin.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received Third-rank meiren janggin.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 上欲臨其喪，諸貝勒諫止，賜御服以斂。

translations.literal: The khan wished to attend his funeral; the beile remonstrated and stopped it; imperial robes were bestowed for the encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wished to attend his funeral but was dissuaded; imperial robes were sent for burial.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，改世職三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi the hereditary office was changed to Third-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 the hereditary rank became Third-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 三傳，降襲。

translations.literal: After three transmissions the inheritance was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After three generations the rank was lowered.

sentences.zh: 揚古利從弟譚泰，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yangguli's younger cousin Tantai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tantai, Yangguli's cousin, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 譚泰弟譚布，天聰初，為巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Tantai's younger brother Tanbu in early Tiancong was bayara jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Tanbu, Tantai's brother, was bayara jalan janggin early in Tiancong.

sentences.zh: 五年，從伐明，圍大凌河城，城人出樵採，率先邀擊，斬三人，俘二人，復與希福等擊敗明援兵自錦州至者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the campaign against the Ming and besieged Dalinhe; townspeople came out to gather firewood; he was first to intercept, beheaded three, captured two, and again with Xifu and others defeated Ming relief from Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalinhe he intercepted wood-gatherers, killed three, and beat Jinzhou relief with Xifu.

sentences.zh: 崇德三年，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde he was appointed councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he became councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，與薩穆什喀、索海等伐索倫部，取道虎爾哈部，攻雅克薩城，得丁壯三百餘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, with Samushka and Suohai and others he campaigned against the Solon, by way of the Hūrka tribe attacked Yaksa city, and took more than three hundred able-bodied men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he took Yaksa on the Solon campaign with Samushka and three hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 索倫部長博穆博果爾迎戰，擊卻之，護所俘以歸。

translations.literal: Solon chief Bomboguo'er met them in battle; they beat him back and escorted the captives home.
translations.idiomatic: Bomboguo'er fought them off but they brought the prisoners home.

sentences.zh: 授牛錄章京，賜貂皮及人戶。

translations.literal: He was granted niru janggin and given sable pelts and households.
translations.idiomatic: He received niru janggin, sables, and households.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢，明兵驟至，殘屯丁，論罰如例。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted —; Ming troops suddenly arrived and slaughtered garrison laborers; he was fined as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ming raiders killed garrison laborers and he was fined.

sentences.zh: 六年，？

translations.literal: In the sixth year —
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year —

sentences.zh: 十六大臣。

translations.literal: he was among the sixteen great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: he became one of sixteen great ministers.

sentences.zh: 時我兵屯田義州，譚布及覺善率兵為伐明，圍錦州。

translations.literal: At that time our troops farmed at Yizhou; Tanbu and Jueshan led troops in the Ming campaign besieging Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While troops farmed at Yizhou, Tanbu and Jueshan besieged Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明總兵祖大壽以步卒出戰，譚布衝堅力戰，复敗其騎卒，斬材官一以徇。

translations.literal: Ming Commander Zu Dashou led foot soldiers out to fight; Tanbu charged strong places and again defeated his cavalry, beheading one supply officer as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou sallied; Tanbu broke foot and horse and beheaded a supply officer.

sentences.zh: 明總督洪承疇來援，譚布從其兄譚泰迎戰，敵騎至，譚布屢奮戰挫敵。

translations.literal: Ming Governor Hong Chengchou came to relieve; Tanbu with his brother Tantai met the fight; when enemy cavalry arrived Tanbu repeatedly fought and checked them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Chengchou relieved, Tanbu with Tantai repeatedly checked the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以功，加半個前程。

translations.literal: For merit he was given half a frontier honor.
translations.idiomatic: He received half a frontier honor.

sentences.zh: 祖大壽既降，上命諸大臣與較射，賞諸中侯者，譚布賜駝一。

translations.literal: After Zu Dashou surrendered, the khan ordered great ministers to compete in archery and rewarded those who hit the target; Tanbu was given one camel.
translations.idiomatic: After Dashou's surrender Tanbu won a camel at the archery contest.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，復與覺善戍錦州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he again garrisoned Jinzhou with Jueshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's first month he garrisoned Jinzhou with Jueshan.

sentences.zh: 九月，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗伐明，略寧遠。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Prince Zheng Jirhala against the Ming and raided Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he raided Ningyuan with Jirhala.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，擊李自成，追至慶都，進二等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes, struck Li Zicheng, pursued to Qingdu, and was advanced to Second-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he crossed the passes, chased Li Zicheng to Qingdu, and rose to Second-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 二年，從饒餘郡王阿巴泰鎮山東，與準塔徇徐州，擊敗明軍，得舟五百餘、砲五十有七。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince Raoyu Abatai in garrisoning Shandong; with Zhuntai he raided Xuzhou, defeated Ming troops, and took more than five hundred boats and fifty-seven cannon.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year at Xuzhou he took five hundred boats and fifty-seven guns.

sentences.zh: 時豫親王多鐸下江南，自泗州渡河趨揚州，而明總兵劉澤清、總漕田仰猶保淮安，譚布與準塔師至清江浦，澤清、仰皆走，遂定淮安，下如皋、通州，撫輯附近諸州縣。

translations.literal: While Prince Yu Dodo went south into Jiangnan from Sizhou toward Yangzhou, Ming commanders Liu Zeqing and Tian Yang still held Huai'an; Tanbu and Zhuntai reached Qingjiangpu; Zeqing and Yang fled; Huai'an was pacified; Rugao and Tongzhou were taken and nearby prefectures and counties were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tanbu and Zhuntai took Huai'an while Liu Zeqing fled, then Rugao and Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 進一等甲喇章京，加半個前程。

translations.literal: He was advanced to First-rank jalan janggin with half a frontier honor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to First-rank jalan janggin with half a frontier honor.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格擊張獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fought Zhang Xianzhong with Prince Su.

sentences.zh: 出城？

translations.literal: Leaving the city —
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the city —

sentences.zh: 六年，從端重親王博洛討姜瓖，圍大同。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo against Jiang Xiang and besieged Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he besieged Datong with Bolo against Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 瓖潛結援賊倚北山綴我軍，而自糾為；

translations.literal: Jiang secretly linked relief bandits on the northern hills to pin our army while he gathered strength himself;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang tied up our forces with northern relief while rallying his own;

sentences.zh: 又分兵徇太原、？

translations.literal: again he divided troops toward Taiyuan —
translations.idiomatic: he also sent columns toward Taiyuan —

sentences.zh: 夾擊。

translations.literal: in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 譚布與鰲拜、車爾布等先破賊援，還擊瓖，迫使入城，斬殪甚平陽、汾州。

translations.literal: Tanbu with Oboi, Che'erbu, and others first broke the rebel relief, then turned back on Jiang, forced him into the city, and beheaded many; Pingyang and Fenzhou were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tanbu with Oboi broke Jiang's relief, drove him into Datong, and pacified Pingyang and Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 論功，遇恩詔，累進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit, on an imperial grace amnesty, he was repeatedly advanced to First-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and grace amnesty raised him to First-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month's third month he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，譚泰誅，詔兄弟毋連坐。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month Tantai was executed; an edict said brothers were not to be punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: When Tantai was executed that August, brothers were spared collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋罷尚書，復為三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed as minister and restored as Third-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the ministry and returned to Third-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 4.

sentences.zh: 薩穆什喀，佟佳氏，扈爾漢第三弟也。

translations.literal: Samushka, of the Tonggiya clan, was Hurhan's third younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Samushka of Tonggiya was Hurhan's third brother.

sentences.zh: 隸滿洲正白旗。

translations.literal: He belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 少從太祖轉戰，積功授游擊。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Taizu on campaign and, for accumulated merit, was appointed guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Taizu from youth and became guerrilla officer.

sentences.zh: 嘗以十二人逐敵山麓，斬百人，獲五十三人，馬、牛、羊千計。

translations.literal: Once with twelve men he pursued the enemy in the foothills, beheaded a hundred, captured fifty-three, and took more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: With twelve men he killed a hundred, took fifty-three prisoners, and seized a thousand head of stock.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，列十六大臣，佐鑲白旗。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded he was listed among the sixteen great ministers assisting the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession he was one of sixteen ministers for the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，從伐明，攻灤州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against the Ming and attacked Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 he attacked Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，復從貝勒岳託等伐明，規取旅順。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again followed Beile Yoto and others against the Ming, planning to take Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Yoto's plan to take Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 時師自陸行，舍馬徒行。

translations.literal: At that time the army marched by land and abandoned horses to go on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The column went on foot and left its horses.

sentences.zh: 至水次，岳託勉薩穆什？

translations.literal: Reaching the water, Yoto urged Samushka —
translations.idiomatic: At the shore Yoto urged Samushka —

sentences.zh: 皆乘馬，薩穆什喀曰：「師潛進，安用乘馬為？

translations.literal: all to mount horses; Samushka said, "The army advances in secret—what use are horses?"
translations.idiomatic: to ride; Samushka said a secret march needed no horses.

sentences.zh: 」乃率喀努力，薩穆什喀對曰：「如貝勒言。

translations.literal: He then led Kenu'er; Samushka answered, "As the beile says.
translations.idiomatic: He led Kenu'er and answered, "As you say, beile.

sentences.zh: 此城誓必下，不空歸也！

translations.literal: This city must be taken—I shall not return empty!"
translations.idiomatic: This city must fall—I will not come back empty!"

sentences.zh: 」遂與白奇超哈章京巴奇蘭以舟先，身被百創，戰益厲，遂破旅順。

translations.literal: He then with baqi chao janggin Baqilan went ahead by boat; he suffered a hundred wounds yet fought fiercer and broke Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: With Baqilan he went first by boat, took a hundred wounds, and stormed Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 師還，太宗郊勞，親酌金？

translations.literal: When the army returned Hong Taiji welcomed him in the suburbs and personally poured golden — as reward and advanced him to First-rank assistant general.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Taiji feasted him in the suburbs, poured gold wine, and made him First-rank assistant general.

sentences.zh: 以賜，進一等參將。

translations.literal: For reward he was advanced to First-rank assistant general.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to First-rank assistant general.

sentences.zh: 八，取？

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took —
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took —

sentences.zh: 年，授甲喇額真。

translations.literal: In that year he was appointed jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 從貝勒杜蘭戍海州。

translations.literal: He followed Beile Dulan in garrisoning Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Haizhou with Beile Dulan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命副巴奇蘭伐黑龍江虎爾哈部，降其其地。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was deputy to Baqilan in campaigning against the Hūrka of the Amur, reducing their territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he joined Baqilan against Amur Hūrka and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，師還。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned in the fourth month of the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 加三等梅​​勒章京，授白奇超哈章京。

translations.literal: He was given Third-rank meiren janggin and appointed baqi chao janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He received Third-rank meiren janggin and baqi chao janggin.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從武英郡王阿濟格等伐明，入長城，與額駙蘇納帥師攻容城，先登，克之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Ying Ajige and others against the Ming, entered the Great Wall, and with Imperial Son-in-law Suna commanded the attack on Rongcheng, first to ascend and take it.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he entered the Wall with Ajige and was first up at Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 復從武英郡王阿濟格攻皮島，督擺牙喇兵渡江，先至岸，與固山額真阿山、葉臣等共攻克之，斬其守將沈世魁，進二等。

translations.literal: Again he followed Prince Ying Ajige in attacking Pidao, supervised bayara troops crossing the river, was first ashore, and with Gushan Ejen Ashan and Yechen jointly took it and beheaded defender Shen Shikui; he was advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Pidao first with Ashan and Yechen, killed Shen Shikui, and rose one grade.

sentences.zh: 七月，授工部承政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四年，與刑部承政索海分將左右翼伐索倫部，部人達爾布尼、阿哈木都戶、白庫都、漢必爾代據厄庫爾城拒我師，薩穆什喀合左右翼攻克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with Punishments Minister Suohai dividing left and right wings against the Solon, when Dalbuni, Ahumudu, Baikudu, and Hanbierdai held Ekur city, Samushka joined both wings and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he and Suohai took Ekur from the Solon chiefs.

sentences.zh: 進攻鐸陳，未下，牛錄額真薩必圖等引兵助攻，鐸陳、阿撒津二城兵潛出邀戰，薩穆什喀設伏敗之，斬七十人。

translations.literal: Pressing Duochen, it was not taken; Niru Ejen Sabitu and others led troops to assist; troops of Duochen and Asajin cities slipped out to intercept; Samushka set an ambush, defeated them, and beheaded seventy.
translations.idiomatic: At Duochen he ambushed a sortie and killed seventy.

sentences.zh: 五年，師還，上郊勞賜宴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the army returned, the khan welcomed them in the suburbs with a feast.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the khan feasted the returning army in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 吏議薩穆什喀伐索倫，得三屯，复叛，其長博穆博果爾掠正藍旗輜重，坐視不救，當削職、籍沒，上命削職，貰籍沒。

translations.literal: The ministry held that on the Solon campaign three settlements were taken then rebelled, and chief Bomboguo'er plundered the Plain Blue Banner baggage train while Samushka watched without rescue; he should be stripped and his property registered; the khan ordered office stripped but spared registration.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry would strip him for letting Bomboguo'er loot a train; the khan stripped office only.

sentences.zh: 薩穆什喀陳辯：「博穆博果爾掠輜重，率兵追擊里許，乃與右翼索海等兵遇，索海等攘功。

translations.literal: Samushka argued: "When Bomboguo'er looted the baggage train I pursued several li before meeting Suohai's right wing, and Suohai and others seized the credit."
translations.idiomatic: Samushka claimed he had pursued the looters before Suohai stole the credit.

sentences.zh: 」上命王、貝勒、議政大臣勘覈，以薩穆什喀言妄，論死，上特宥之。

translations.literal: The khan ordered princes, beile, and councilors to investigate; Samushka's words were held false and he was sentenced to death; the khan specially spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators found him lying; he was condemned but spared.

sentences.zh: 复追論戍海州時備不嚴，屯丁為敵殺，論罰鍰。

translations.literal: Again he was reviewed for lax defense when garrisoning Haizhou and garrison laborers were killed by the enemy; he was fined.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined again for deaths among Haizhou garrison laborers.

sentences.zh: 七年，從伐明，攻錦州，敵犯塞，薩穆什喀力戰，敵三至三卻。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the campaign against the Ming and attacked Jinzhou; the enemy violated the borderworks; Samushka fought hard and the enemy three times came and three times retreated.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou he fought off three enemy assaults on the works.

sentences.zh: 錦州下，复授世職牛錄章京。

translations.literal: After Jinzhou fell he was again granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinzhou he received hereditary niru janggin again.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 子羅什，襲職。

translations.literal: His son Luoshi succeeded to the office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoshi inherited.

sentences.zh: 雅賴，扈爾漢第七弟也。

translations.literal: Yalai was Hurhan's seventh younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yalai was Hurhan's seventh brother.

sentences.zh: 事太祖，從伐烏喇，略地朝鮮，數被創。

translations.literal: He served Taizu, followed campaigns against Ula, raided Korean territory, and was wounded many times.
translations.idiomatic: He served Taizu against Ula and Korea and took many wounds.

sentences.zh: 從攻遼東，破蒙古兵。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Liaodong, he broke Mongol troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaodong he broke Mongol forces.

sentences.zh: 從伐察哈爾，先登殺敵。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against the Chakhar, he was first to ascend and kill the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Chakhar he was first up and killed the foe.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年五月，與甲喇額真羅璧等將千人略明新城路，遇毛文，殺九千？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tiancong, with Jalan Ejen Luobi and others he led a thousand men to raid the Ming New Town route; he met Mao Wen —
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he raided the New Town route and met Mao Wen —

sentences.zh: 龍舊部採參者，斬六十人，毀其舟。

translations.literal: long's old troops gathering ginseng; he beheaded sixty and destroyed their boats.
translations.idiomatic: long's foragers, killed sixty, and burned their boats.

sentences.zh: 九月，從揚古利逐逃人雅爾古，复遇文龍部六百餘人，獲千總三及從者十六。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Yangguli in pursuing fugitives to Ya'ergu and again met more than six hundred of Wenlong's troops, capturing three qianzong and sixteen followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he took three qianzong and sixteen men from Wenlong's band.

sentences.zh: 十一月，太宗伐明，薄明都，袁崇煥來援，攻擺牙喇兵，城兵出應，雅賴力戰？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Hong Taiji campaigned against the Ming and pressed the capital; Yuan Chonghuan came to relieve and attacked the bayara troops; city troops sallied in support; Yalai fought fiercely —
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Yuan Chonghuan relieved; Yalai fought fiercely —

sentences.zh: 之。

translations.literal: and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 五年，從攻大凌河，屢勝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the attack on Dalinhe with repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalinhe he won repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 嘗單騎入敵陣，出戰死者屍。

translations.literal: Once he rode alone into the enemy formation and brought out the bodies of dead soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He once rode alone into the enemy lines to recover the dead.

sentences.zh: 七年，取旅順口，與薩穆什喀同舟先濟，敵據岸列陣以拒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he took Lüshunkou; with Samushka he crossed in the same boat first; the enemy held the bank in battle order to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Lüshunkou he and Samushka crossed first while the enemy held the shore.

sentences.zh: 雅賴超躍登岸，大呼曰：「雅賴先登矣！

translations.literal: Yalai leaped ashore and shouted, "Yalai has landed first!"
translations.idiomatic: Yalai sprang ashore shouting, "Yalai is first ashore!"

sentences.zh: 」遂入敵陣。

translations.literal: "—and entered the enemy formation.
translations.idiomatic: "—and charged into the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 黎明，與敵戰，入城被創，戰益奮，我兵或少卻，輒手刃之。

translations.literal: At dawn he fought the enemy; entering the city he was wounded yet fought fiercer; whenever our troops gave ground he cut down the men himself.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fought into the city wounded; if any man fell back he killed him himself.

sentences.zh: 城下，授世職備禦。

translations.literal: Below the walls he was granted the hereditary office of beiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Below the walls he received hereditary beiyu.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde he was appointed councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 2 he became councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 八年，加半個前程。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given half a frontier honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he received half a frontier honor.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從入關，擊李自成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes and struck Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he crossed the passes against Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，從破自成兵潼關，定河南、江南。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in breaking Li Zicheng's troops at Tongguan and pacifying Henan and Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he helped break Li at Tongguan and pacify Henan and the south.

sentences.zh: 論功，遇恩詔，進一等阿思哈尼哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: For merit, on an imperial grace amnesty, he was advanced to First-rank Ashaniyahan with tosoroha.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and grace amnesty raised him to First-rank Ashaniyahan with tosoroha.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's third month he became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四月，坐駐防河間，牛錄額真碩爾對訐告發餉不均，罷，並削拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, for garrisoning Hejian when Niru Ejen Shuo'erdu accused him of unequal rations, he was dismissed and tosoroha was also stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was dismissed from Hejian over ration disputes and lost tosoroha.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 3.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封三等男。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong the fief was fixed as Third-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Qianlong the rank was Third-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 洪尼雅喀，吳扎庫氏，世居噶哈里。

translations.literal: Hongniyaka, of the Wuzhaku clan, long dwelt at Gahari.
translations.idiomatic: Hongniyaka of Wuzhaku came from Gahari.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起時，扈倫諸部方強，烏喇尤橫肆，聞洪尼雅喀以材武豪於所部，劫其孥，迫使歸附。

translations.literal: When Taizu first rose, the Hurun tribes were still strong and Ula especially overbearing; hearing Hongniyaka was famed for martial prowess in his tribe, they seized his family and forced him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu rose, Ula seized Hongniyaka's family to force his submission.

sentences.zh: 洪尼雅喀既偕往，念烏喇貝勒不足事，中途棄，隸滿州鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: Hongniyaka went along, but seeing the Ula beile unworthy of service, he abandoned them midway and was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He went, then left Ula midway and entered the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 走；

translations.literal: fled;
translations.idiomatic: fled;

sentences.zh: 與弟薩蘇喀、薩穆唐阿率其族四十人歸太祖。

translations.literal: with his younger brothers Sasuka and Samutang'a he led forty clansmen to submit to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: with Sasuka and Samutang'a he brought forty clansmen to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 授牛錄額真，俾領其天命三年，從伐明有功，擢甲喇額真。

translations.literal: He was appointed niru ejen and put in command of them; in the third year of Tianming he followed the campaign against the Ming with merit and was promoted to jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He became niru ejen; in Tianming 3 he fought the Ming and rose to jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 天聰二年，太宗自將伐明，攻錦州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancong Hong Taiji personally led a campaign against the Ming and attacked Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 2 Hong Taiji personally besieged Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 師薄城，洪尼雅死，洪？

translations.literal: When the army pressed the city, Hongniyaka was first to ascend, destroyed the parapet, fell and injured his foot; the enemy pressed him and were about to seize and bind him;
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou he was first up, wrecked the wall, fell and was nearly taken;

sentences.zh: 喀先登，毀其堞，墜傷足，敵迫之，將執而縶焉，季弟薩穆唐阿以壯達從軍，馳護尼雅喀乃免。

translations.literal: his youngest brother Samutang'a, a dartachi on campaign, galloped to protect Hongniyaka and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Samutang'a rode in and saved him.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，授世職三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was granted the hereditary office of Third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's fifth month he received Third-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 子武拉禪。

translations.literal: His son Wulacan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wulacan.

sentences.zh: 武拉禪襲世職。

translations.literal: Wulacan inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Wulacan inherited.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授擺牙喇甲喇額真。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed bayara jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he became bayara jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 十月，從豫親王多鐸西討李自成。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he followed Prince Yu Dodo west against Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined Dodo's western campaign against Li Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，至潼關，甫立營，賊掩至，擊？

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when the army reached Tongguan and had just pitched camp, bandits rushed up —
translations.idiomatic: At Tongguan, as camp was pitched, rebels rushed in —

sentences.zh: 之。

translations.literal: he struck them down.
translations.idiomatic: he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二年，從端重親王博洛下浙江，趨平湖，敗敵，獲來攻，武拉禪與戰於赭山、於硃橋、於範村，屢勝？

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo into Zhejiang toward Pinghu, defeated the enemy, and when attackers came, Wulacan fought at Zhushan, Zhuqiao, and Fancun with repeated victories —
translations.idiomatic: In the second year in Zhejiang he won at Zhushan, Zhuqiao, and Fancun —

sentences.zh: 戰艦。

translations.literal: against war junks.
translations.idiomatic: against war junks.

sentences.zh: 進略杭州，馬士英、方國安擁。

translations.literal: Advancing on Hangzhou, Ma Shiying and Fang Guo'an held —
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou he faced Ma Shiying and Fang Guo'an —

sentences.zh: 四年，授鑲紅旗蒙古梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Mongol meiren ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Mongol meiren ejen of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，增設滄州、大名駐防，命武拉禪以梅勒額真駐大名。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year garrisons were added at Cangzhou and Daming; Wulacan was ordered as meiren ejen to garrison Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year's first month he garrisoned Daming.

sentences.zh: 金聲桓為亂，從征南大將軍譚泰攻南昌，五合五勝。

translations.literal: When Jin Shenghuan rebelled he followed Pacification-of-the-South Grand General Tantai in attacking Nanchang; five engagements, five victories.
translations.idiomatic: Against Jin Shenghuan at Nanchang he won five fights in five meetings.

sentences.zh: 聲桓以步騎七萬拒戰，率本旗兵合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shenghuan met him with seventy thousand foot and horse; Wulacan led his banner in the combined attack and thoroughly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shenghuan brought seventy thousand men; Wulacan broke them.

sentences.zh: 聲桓既死，剿餘寇於袁州，擊敗明將硃翊鏦，定府一、縣二。

translations.literal: After Shenghuan died he mopped up remnant bandits at Yuanzhou, defeated Ming Commander Zhu Yicong, and pacified one prefecture and two counties.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenghuan's death he cleared Yuanzhou and took one prefecture and two counties.

sentences.zh: 千人；

translations.literal: A thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: A thousand men;

sentences.zh: 別遣甲喇？

translations.literal: he separately dispatched jalan —
translations.idiomatic: he sent a jalan detachment —

sentences.zh: 六年七月，有趙鳳岡者，為亂於畿南，武拉禪討之，斬鳳岡，殲其額真哈其哈等擊賊寶山村，獲其渠田東樓、楊牌子。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year a Zhao Fenggang stirred trouble in southern Jizhou; Wulacan suppressed him and beheaded Fenggang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's seventh month he killed Zhao Fenggang in southern Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was appointed vice minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year's fifth month he became vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 功，遇恩詔，世職屢進，尋定為二等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit, on an imperial grace amnesty, his hereditary office was repeatedly advanced and finally fixed as Second-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: Grace amnesties raised him to Second-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從寧海大將軍宜爾德攻舟山，明將陳六禦等以三萬人拒戰，武拉禪督纛奮擊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Pacification-of-the-Sea Grand General Yierde in attacking Zhoushan; Ming Commander Chen Liuyu and others met him with thirty thousand men; Wulacan commanded the banner and struck fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year at Zhoushan he charged Chen Liuyu's thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 以功，進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to First-rank Ashaniyahan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he rose to First-rank Ashaniyahan.

sentences.zh: 復以恩詔，加拖沙喇哈番阿拉那於市，武拉禪勘獄，反罪阿拉那，坐？

translations.literal: Again on an imperial grace amnesty he added tosoroha Alana; when Alana was tried in the market Wulacan investigated and instead convicted Alana; he was punished —
translations.idiomatic: He added tosoroha Alana, then convicted Alana at trial and was punished —

sentences.zh: 內大臣額爾克戴青家奴毆侍？

translations.literal: Inner Minister Erke Daiqing's household slave beat attendants —
translations.idiomatic: Erke Daiqing's slave beat attendants —

sentences.zh: 十六年，領侍枉抑，削所加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, as attendant minister he wrongly suppressed a case and the added tosoroha was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he lost his added tosoroha for bending a case.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以病免。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was excused for illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年十月，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Kangxi 6.

sentences.zh: 薩蘇喀，洪尼雅喀仲弟也。

translations.literal: Sasuka was Hongniyaka's second younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sasuka was Hongniyaka's second brother.

sentences.zh: 事太祖，授擺牙喇甲喇額真。

translations.literal: He served Taizu and was appointed bayara jalan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: He served Taizu as bayara jalan ejen.

sentences.zh: 天命七年，從太祖伐明，攻廣寧，戰於沙嶺。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianming he followed Taizu against the Ming and attacked Guangning; battle was at Shaling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 7 he fought at Shaling in the Guangning campaign.

sentences.zh: 我師有都爾根者，馬蹶，敵騎三共取之，兩刃交下，薩蘇喀馳入敵陣，躍馬大呼，斬一人，排一人撲地，遂翼之出，無敢逼者。

translations.literal: In our army a man Durgen had his horse stumble; three enemy horsemen together seized him and two blades struck down together; Sasuka galloped into the enemy ranks, leaped his horse, shouted, beheaded one, knocked one to the ground, and thus winged him out; none dared press close.
translations.idiomatic: When Durgen was down under three swords, Sasuka charged in, killed one, knocked one down, and pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，從太宗伐明，薄明都，薩蘇喀為前驅偵敵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong he followed Hong Taiji against the Ming and pressed the capital; Sasuka was vanguard scouting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he scouted ahead at the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，師圍大凌河城，城兵突出，薩蘇喀率兵追擊，及壕而返；

translations.literal: In the fifth year the army besieged Dalinhe; city troops sallied; Sasuka led troops in pursuit to the moat and returned;
translations.idiomatic: At Dalinhe he chased a sortie to the moat;

sentences.zh: 城兵尋复，從噶布什賢噶喇昂邦勞薩擊敗寧遠兵，獲馬二十有？

translations.literal: city troops sallied again; following gabushixian galaa angbang Laosa he defeated Ningyuan troops and captured more than twenty horses —
translations.idiomatic: again with Laosa he beat Ningyuan troops and took twenty horses —

sentences.zh: 出，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: sallied out again and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: and beat them again when they sallied.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，略明前屯二。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he raided the two Qiantun posts of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year's second month he raided the two Qiantun posts.

sentences.zh: ，敵三百屯城外，奮擊，敵潰走，逐之至城下，斬獲甚？

translations.literal: —, three hundred enemy held outside the walls; he struck fiercely; the enemy broke and fled; pursued to beneath the walls; beheaded and captured very many —
translations.idiomatic: — three hundred Ming outside the walls were routed with many heads taken —

sentences.zh: 六月，師至大同，以三十人偵左。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the army reached Datong; with thirty men he scouted the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month at Datong he scouted with thirty men.

sentences.zh: 九年，從貝勒多爾袞招察哈爾林丹汗子額哲，進略明邊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Beile Dorgon to receive Lindan Khan's son Erkezhe and advanced raiding the Ming frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he raided the Ming frontier with Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 固山額真圖爾格設伏敗敵，敵？

translations.literal: Gushan Ejen Turgut set an ambush and defeated the enemy; the enemy —
translations.idiomatic: Turgut ambushed and beat the enemy; the enemy —

sentences.zh: 潰走，薩蘇喀躡其後，斬級最，授半個前程。

translations.literal: fled in disorder; Sasuka followed behind and took the most heads; he was granted half a frontier honor.
translations.idiomatic: fled; Sasuka took the most heads and received half a frontier honor.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部參政。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 崇德二年，與甲喇額真丹岱等以八十人略明邊，次清河，敵七百屯守，與戰大勝，獲纛二、馬二十餘。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongde, with Jalan Ejen Dantai and others, eighty men raided the Ming frontier and halted at Qinghe; seven hundred enemy held defense; they fought a great victory and captured two banners and more than twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 2 eighty men raided to Qinghe, beat seven hundred Ming, and took two banners.

sentences.zh: 五年，圍錦州，守，戰比有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he besieged Jinzhou and in defense and battle had merit throughout.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth-year Jinzhou siege he fought with merit throughout.

sentences.zh: 順治初，擢鑲紅旗？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was promoted to the Bordered Red Banner —
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi he rose in the Bordered Red Banner —

sentences.zh: 木魯河。

translations.literal: Mulu River.
translations.idiomatic: at the Mulu River.

sentences.zh: 六年，圍松山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he besieged Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he besieged Songshan.

sentences.zh: 八年，攻寧遠，取中後所、前屯滿洲梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attacked Ningyuan, took Zhonghousuo and Qiantun, and became Manchu meiren ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took Zhonghousuo and Qiantun and became Manchu meiren ejen.

sentences.zh: 從入關，擊李自成，與梅勒額真和託共驅入敵營，中砲沒，贈三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: He followed the entry through the passes against Li Zicheng; with Meiren Ejen Hotuo he together drove into the enemy camp; struck by cannon he died in battle; posthumously granted Third-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the passes against Li Zicheng, he charged with Hotuo, was killed by cannon, and was posthumously Third-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 阿山，伊爾根覺羅氏，世居穆溪。

translations.literal: Ashan, of the Irgen Gioro clan, long dwelt at Muxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan of Irgen Gioro came from Muxi.

sentences.zh: 父阿爾塔什，率阿山及諸子阿達海、濟爾垓、噶賴，以七村附太祖。

translations.literal: His father Altashi led Ashan and his sons Adahai, Jiergai, and Galai, with seven villages, to submit to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Altashi brought Ashan, Adahai, Jiergai, Galai, and seven villages to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖妻以同族女兄弟，號「額駙」，而以阿山等屬貝勒代善。

translations.literal: Taizu married him to a clanswoman of the same lineage and styled him "imperial son-in-law," placing Ashan and the others under Beile Daisan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu married him to a kinswoman, styled him imperial son-in-law, and placed him under Daisan.

sentences.zh: 代善置閒散，觖望，與諸弟及其子塞赫等逃之明。

translations.literal: Daisan kept them idle; resentful, Ashan with his brothers and his son Saihe and others fled to the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Idle under Daisan, Ashan fled to the Ming with his brothers and son Saihe.

sentences.zh: 上收其孥，貝勒阿敏以兵追之，射殪阿山二子，阿山亦被創，兄弟相失。

translations.literal: The khan seized their families; Beile Amin pursued with troops, shot and killed two of Ashan's sons; Ashan was also wounded and the brothers were separated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu seized their families; Amin pursued, killed two of Ashan's sons, and wounded Ashan.

sentences.zh: 穆克譚追射阿達海，阿達海斫穆克譚，墜馬幾死，遂奪其馬，與阿山等入明邊，尋復自歸。

translations.literal: Muketan shot at Adahai; Adahai cut Muketan down; Muketan nearly fell from his horse; he seized the horse and with Ashan and others entered Ming territory, then soon returned of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Adahai wounded Muketan, took his horse, entered Ming lands, then returned.

sentences.zh: 太祖問其故，對曰：「舉族相投，矢？

translations.literal: Taizu asked the reason; he answered, "Our whole clan came over—did we pledge our lives only to fill the border garrison?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked why; he said his clan had not come merely to garrison the frontier.

sentences.zh: 命疆埸，豈直充？

translations.literal: Are we only to serve as —
translations.idiomatic: Were they only to be —

sentences.zh: 役乎？

translations.literal: corvée labor?"
translations.idiomatic: corvée?"

sentences.zh: 」乃置諸左右。

translations.literal: He was then placed among the close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept at court.

sentences.zh: 旗制定，隸滿洲正藍旗。

translations.literal: When the banners were fixed he was enrolled in the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，從伐遼陽，授二等參將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming he followed the taking of Liaoyang and was appointed Second-rank assistant general.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 6 at Liaoyang he became Second-rank assistant general.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，旗置大臣一為將，其次置大臣二為佐，又其次置大臣二備調遣。

translations.literal: When Hong Taiji acceded, each banner had one minister as commander, next two as assistants, and next two in reserve for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Taiji's accession each banner had layered command posts.

sentences.zh: 使阿山佐正白旗，阿達海與同旗備調遣。

translations.literal: Ashan was made assistant to the Plain White Banner; Adahai was reserve dispatch for the same banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan assisted the Plain White Banner; Adahai was reserve dispatch.

sentences.zh: 是歲，貝勒代善等帥師伐扎魯特部，上令阿山與冷格里以兵六百入喀爾喀巴林部逐邏卒，縱火張軍威。

translations.literal: That year Beile Daisan and others led troops against the Zhalut tribe; the khan ordered Ashan with Lenggeri and six hundred men into Khalkha Balin to drive border guards, set fires to display army strength.
translations.idiomatic: That year Ashan with Lenggeri raided Balin with six hundred men and burned the steppe to show force.

sentences.zh: 師還，進三等副將。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was advanced to Third-rank deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: On return he rose to Third-rank deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，從伐朝鮮，克義州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against Korea and took Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he took Korean Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 阿達海坐匿太祖御用兜鍪，鞭五十。

translations.literal: Adahai was punished with fifty lashes for concealing Taizu's personal helmet.
translations.idiomatic: Adahai was flogged fifty strokes for hiding Taizu's helmet.

sentences.zh: 又違上命，為貝勒多鐸媒聘國舅阿布泰女，論死，上宥之，命奪官，籍其家之半。

translations.literal: Again disobeying orders, he acted as go-between for Beile Dodo in betrothing Grand Secretary Abu Tai's daughter; sentenced to death, the khan spared him, ordered office taken, and half his household registered.
translations.idiomatic: Adahai brokered Dodo's marriage against orders, was condemned but spared and lost half his property.

sentences.zh: 阿達海託言捕魚，以十騎逾赫圖阿喇城遁，克徹尼追之還。

translations.literal: Adahai pretended to fish and with ten riders fled beyond Hetuala city; Kecheni pursued and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Adahai fled fishing beyond Hetuala; Kecheni caught him.

sentences.zh: 阿達海私語從人曰：「我欲亂箭射殺克徹尼，如爾輩何！

translations.literal: Adahai privately told followers, "I mean to kill Kecheni in a volley of arrows—what of the likes of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Adahai vowed to kill Kecheni with arrows.

sentences.zh: 」語聞，上命誅之。

translations.literal: When the words were heard, the khan ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The khan had him executed when this was heard.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，阿山復與弟噶賴子塞赫及阿達海子查塔、莫洛渾奔明寧遠，上收其孥，遣兵往追之，阿山等將入明境，遣從者先，明守塞兵執而殺之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year Ashan again with his younger brother Galai's son Saihe and Adahai's sons Zhata and Molohun fled to Ming Ningyuan; the khan seized their families and sent troops in pursuit; Ashan and the others, about to enter Ming territory, sent followers ahead; Ming border guards seized and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third autumn Ashan fled toward Ningyuan; Ming guards killed his advance party.

sentences.zh: 阿山等懼，復還，請罪，上复宥之，還其孥，使復職。

translations.literal: Ashan and the others feared, returned, begged pardon; the khan again spared them, restored their families, and reinstated them.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back, were pardoned, and restored.

sentences.zh: 阿山乃訐雅蓀與同謀，雅蓀者起微賤，以葉赫攻兀扎魯城時，戰有功，太祖寵任之，雅蓀矢言殉太祖。

translations.literal: Ashan then accused Yagun of complicity; Yagun rose from humble rank; when Yehe attacked Wuzhalu city he had battle merit; Taizu favored him; Yagun vowed to die with Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan denounced Yagun, once a favorite who had vowed to die with Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，不果殉，臨喪慢。

translations.literal: When Taizu died he did not in fact follow him in death and was disrespectful at the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu's death Yagun did not follow him in death and was rude at the mourning.

sentences.zh: 至是，鞫得實，​​遂坐誅。

translations.literal: At this time investigation proved true and he was condemned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved it and Yagun was executed.

sentences.zh: 冬，從上伐明，克洪山口城，薄明都，軍於城東南。

translations.literal: That winter he followed the khan against the Ming, took Hongshankou city, pressed the Ming capital, and encamped southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he took Hongshankou and camped southeast of the Ming capital.

sentences.zh: 阿山與圖魯什週視敵營，請速進攻，上命即夜漏三下列陣，詰旦遂戰，大破明軍，陣斬武經略滿桂等。

translations.literal: Ashan with Turushi circled the enemy camps and asked for a swift attack; the khan ordered arrays drawn at the third watch that night; at dawn battle was joined and the Ming army was thoroughly broken; Military Superintendent Man Gui and others were beheaded in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan and Turushi urged attack; at dawn the Ming were shattered and Man Gui was killed.

sentences.zh: 四年，攻永平，上命阿山及葉臣選部下猛士二十四人，乘夜挾雲梯以攻，諭曰：「登梯當令四人先分立梯端二旁，次令四人登，又次令十六人相繼上，又次則爾曹督其後，復令​​各旗出將一兵千人助攻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he attacked Yongping; the khan ordered Ashan and Yechen to choose twenty-four picked men of their commands, take cloud ladders by night to assault, instructing: "When mounting, four first stand at the ladder ends on either side, next four ascend, next sixteen follow in succession, then you supervise behind; again each banner sends one officer with a thousand men to assist."
translations.idiomatic: At Yongping Taizu ordered Ashan and Yechen to lead twenty-four stormers up cloud ladders by night.

sentences.zh: 」次日，日加寅，薄城樹梯，犯矢石奮戰。

translations.literal: The next day at yin hour they neared the wall, set ladders, and braved arrow and stone in fierce battle.
translations.idiomatic: Next day at dawn they set ladders under fire.

sentences.zh: 俄，城上砲裂藥發，敵兵自驚擾，阿山督所部冒火銳上，諸軍繼進，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Soon powder on the wall exploded; enemy troops were thrown into panic; Ashan led his command through fire in a sharp ascent; the host followed and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the wall powder blew, Ashan led through the flames and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 五年，攻大凌河，率銳騎邏錦州、松山，俘明兵，明守將出援，與勞薩、圖魯什以三二千，斬百餘級，獲纛三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he attacked Dalinhe, led picked cavalry around Jinzhou and Songshan, captured Ming soldiers; Ming defenders sallied in relief; with Laosa and Turushi with two or three thousand they beheaded more than a hundred, took three banners.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalinhe he raided around Jinzhou and Songshan with Laosa and Turushi and took three banners.

sentences.zh: 上勞以金？

translations.literal: The khan rewarded him with gold —
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rewarded him with gold —

sentences.zh: ，尋授固山額真。

translations.literal: and soon appointed him gushan ejen.
translations.idiomatic: and soon made him gushan ejen.

sentences.zh: 六年，上自將伐察哈爾？

translations.literal: In the sixth year the khan personally led a campaign against the Chakhar —
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Taizu campaigned against the Chakhar —

sentences.zh: 百人敗其，阿山與梅勒額真布爾吉方行邊，聞上至西拉木倫河，帥師來會，上命率精騎三百助圖魯什為前驅。

translations.literal: a hundred men defeated them; Ashan and Meiren Ejen Burji were patrolling the frontier; hearing the khan had reached the Xilamuren River, they led troops to join; the khan ordered three hundred picked cavalry to help Turushi as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan and Burji joined Taizu on the Xilamuren with three hundred picked horse for Turushi's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 察哈爾汗遁去，上引還，復命阿山等帥師防邊。

translations.literal: The Chakhar khan fled; the khan turned back and again ordered Ashan and others to command frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chakhar khan fled, Ashan was sent back to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 七年，與布爾吉偵鹿島，多所俘獲。

translations.literal: In the seventh year with Burji he scouted Ludao with many captures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he scouted Ludao with Burji and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 八年，與圖魯什略錦州，貝勒岳託謂圖魯什曰：「軍中調遣，當就阿山商榷，勿違其言。

translations.literal: In the eighth year with Turushi he raided Jinzhou; Beile Yoto told Turushi, "Army dispatch should be discussed with Ashan—do not disobey his words."
translations.idiomatic: At Jinzhou Yoto told Turushi to follow Ashan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 」既，復從伐察哈爾，斬蒙古逃人。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again followed the campaign against the Chakhar and beheaded Mongol fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned against the Chakhar and killed fugitives.

sentences.zh: 追錄克永平功，進三等昂邦章京，免徭役；

translations.literal: Recording his Yongping merit retroactively, he was advanced to Third-rank angbang janggin and exempted from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: For Yongping he received Third-rank angbang janggin and corvée exemption;

sentences.zh: 並分以虎爾哈俘百人，隸所領牛錄。

translations.literal: and a hundred Hūrka captives were divided to the niru under his command.
translations.idiomatic: a hundred Hūrka captives were added to his niru.

sentences.zh: 九年，師入明邊，略山西，明兵自山海關赴援。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the army entered the Ming frontier and raided Shanxi; Ming troops came from Shanhaiguan to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the army raided Shanxi while Ming relief came from Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 上命貝勒多鐸軍廣寧，阿山與固山額真石廷柱率噶布什賢兵四百前驅趨錦州，明副將劉應選等以兵三千五百人來禦，遇於大凌河。

translations.literal: The khan ordered Beile Dodo to hold Guangning; Ashan with Gushan Ejen Shitingzhu led four hundred gabushixian troops as vanguard toward Jinzhou; Ming Vice Commander Liu Yingxuan and others with thirty-five hundred men came to meet them at Dalinhe.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo held Guangning while Ashan with four hundred gabushixian men met Liu Yingxuan at Dalinhe.

sentences.zh: 將戰，多鐸後軍驟至，自山而下，士馬騰踔，軍容甚盛，明兵驚沮。

translations.literal: As battle was about to join, Dodo's rear army suddenly arrived down the hill; men and horses leaped; army bearing was very grand; Ming troops were alarmed and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo's rear appeared on the heights and dismayed the Ming.

sentences.zh: 阿山突起掩擊，我師從之，陣斬應選，殲其兵五百，克台堡一。

translations.literal: Ashan suddenly rose in a flanking strike; our troops followed; Liu Yingxuan was beheaded in the formation; five hundred of his soldiers were annihilated and one platform fort was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan flanked; Liu Yingxuan was killed and five hundred Ming destroyed.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜良馬、鎧甲。

translations.literal: When the army returned, fine horses and armor were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received fine horses and armor.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從武英郡王阿濟格伐明，下鵰鶚、長安嶺二城，率本旗兵獨克東安縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed Prince Ying Ajige against the Ming, took Diaogu and Chang'anling two cities, and with his banner troops alone took Dong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 with Ajige he took Diaogu, Chang'anling, and Dong'an alone.

sentences.zh: 師還，明兵來追，阿山殿，擊斬略盡。

translations.literal: When the army returned Ming troops pursued; Ashan formed the rear guard and struck, beheading nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he rearguarded and cut down the pursuers.

sentences.zh: 二年，取皮島，與葉臣將左翼舟師攻其西北隅，先登，斬守將沈世魁，進一等昂邦章京世職。

translations.literal: In the second year he took Pidao; with Yechen he commanded the left-wing fleet attacking the northwest corner, first to ascend, beheaded defender Shen Shikui, and was advanced to First-rank angbang janggin hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he stormed Pidao first with Yechen, killed Shen Shikui, and rose to First-rank angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，复圍錦州，城兵突圍出攻我師，松山守將潛謀奪火器，阿山迭擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he again besieged Jinzhou; city troops broke out against our army; Songshan defenders secretly plotted to seize firearms; Ashan repeatedly struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the sixth-year Jinzhou siege he repeatedly beat sorties and foiled Songshan plots.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，復從貝勒阿巴泰伐明，入牆子嶺，轉戰至兗州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year he again followed Beile Abatai against the Ming, entered Qiangzileng, and fought through to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year's tenth month he fought through to Yanzhou with Abatai.

sentences.zh: 師還，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, silver and goods were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received silver and gifts.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，擊李自成，自成敗走，阿山偕左翼梅勒額真阿哈尼堪、右翼固山額真馬喇希，濟薄津擊破之，克平陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes against Li Zicheng; when Li was defeated and fled, Ashan with Left Wing Meiren Ejen Ahanikan and Right Wing Gushan Ejen Malaxi crossed the Boping Ford and broke them, taking Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he crossed the Boping Ford with Ahanikan and Malaxi, broke Li Zicheng, and took Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 以功，進三等公。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became Third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 二年，豫親王多鐸自陝西移師下江南，阿山及諸將從。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Yu Dodo shifted his army from Shaanxi south into Jiangnan; Ashan and the generals followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he followed Dodo south from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與馬喇希等取淮河橋，渡淮拔揚州；

translations.literal: With Malaxi and others he took the Huai River bridge, crossed the Huai, and seized Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He took the Huai bridge, crossed, and seized Yangzhou;

sentences.zh: 率舟師溯江上，克江寧，獲明福王。

translations.literal: leading the fleet upriver he took Jiangning and captured the Ming Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: then sailed up the Yangtze, took Jiangning, and captured the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 江南既定，從貝勒博洛、固山額真拜音圖徇浙江，師次杭州，明潞王常淓降。

translations.literal: After Jiangnan was settled he followed Beile Bolo and Gushan Ejen Bayintu into Zhejiang; the army halted at Hangzhou and Ming Prince of Lu Zhu Changfang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After the south fell he entered Zhejiang; the Prince of Lu surrendered at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉興、湖州、紹興、寧波、嚴州皆下。

translations.literal: Jiaxing, Huzhou, Shaoxing, Ningbo, and Yanzhou all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing, Huzhou, Shaoxing, Ningbo, and Yanzhou followed.

sentences.zh: 師還，賚金銀、鞍馬。

translations.literal: When the army returned, gold, silver, saddles, and horses were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On return he received gold, silver, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 阿山自太宗時，屢坐事被論，輒貸之。

translations.literal: From Hong Taiji's time Ashan was repeatedly condemned yet always pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: From Hong Taiji's reign onward Ashan was often condemned yet pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三年，坐妄聽巫者言，罪所部，被訐，罷官，奪世職。

translations.literal: In the third year, for heedlessly listening to a shaman and punishing his command, being denounced, he was dismissed and deprived of hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was dismissed and lost his rank for trusting a shaman.

sentences.zh: 旋复授一等昂邦章京。

translations.literal: Soon he was again granted First-rank angbang janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as First-rank angbang janggin.

sentences.zh: 四年，改一等精奇尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was changed to First-rank Jingqiniha.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the title became First-rank Jingqiniha.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，定封一等男。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong the fief was fixed as First-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: Under early Qianlong the rank was First-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 從弟阿爾津，自有傳。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Aerjin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Aerjin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: ，其子孫皆能以驍勇？

translations.literal: —, their descendants all could fight with fierce courage —
translations.idiomatic: — their descendants all fought with fierce courage —

sentences.zh: 論曰：太祖時，鄰近諸部族歸附，常書兄弟最先，康果禮等最自？

translations.literal: Commentary says: In Taizu's time neighboring tribes submitted; it is commonly written that brothers came first; Kang Guoli and the rest were most self —
translations.idiomatic: The commentary notes that in Taizu's day neighboring tribes submitted, brothers often listed first, and Kang Guoli among the foremost —

sentences.zh: 博爾晉、雅希禪殺敵致果，蓋勞薩、圖魯什之亞也。

translations.literal: Bo'erjin and Yaxishen killed the enemy with fruit—almost the equals of Laosa and Turushi.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'erjin and Yaxishen in killing the enemy rivaled Laosa and Turushi.

sentences.zh: 揚善、冷格里、薩穆什喀皆有戰績，非藉父兄顯者。

translations.literal: Yangshan, Lenggeri, and Samushka all had battle records without relying on fathers or elder brothers for prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Yangshan, Lenggeri, and Samushka won honor without riding fathers' fame.

sentences.zh: 洪尼雅喀尤以材武名。

translations.literal: Hongniyaka was especially famed for martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongniyaka was especially famed for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 阿山屢去復歸，誅弟而用兄，駕馭梟桀，惟恩與法，握其要矣。

translations.literal: Ashan repeatedly left and returned, executed a younger brother yet employed an elder brother—in controlling fierce men he held only to grace and law, and grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Ashan fled and returned, killed one brother and used another; ruling fierce men he balanced grace and law.
